The exact cost depends on the weight distribution of the non-pivot columns of [MATH]. We therefore consider two models: an all-one model, in which every relevant binary coordinate is active, and a Bernoulli[MATH] model, in which the coordinates are independently active with probability [MATH]. For the five Classic McEliece parameter sets, our method reduces the estimated key-recovery cost by [MATH]--[MATH] bits in the all-one model and by [MATH]--[MATH] bits in the Bernoulli[MATH] model.
tldr: The paper accelerates Hemmert's higher-order-vanishing key-recovery attack on Classic McEliece by evaluating the defining kernel sums as truncated upper zeta transforms on the Boolean lattice.
motivation: Kernel computation over the shortened parity-check matrix dominates the cost of Hemmert's key-recovery attack on Classic McEliece, so reducing the cost of the repeated matrix-vector products in the Wiedemann-based kernel computation is the key bottleneck to address.
method: The sums defining the kernel are recast column by column as weighted upper zeta transforms on the Boolean lattice, and only the required band of transform levels between the given level and the lowest needed level is evaluated, yielding exact evaluations of the matrix and its transpose; these truncated transforms are then used inside a Wiedemann-based kernel computation.
result: For the five Classic McEliece parameter sets, the estimated key-recovery cost is reduced by roughly several bits under an all-one activity model and under a Bernoulli activity model, with the exact savings depending on the weight distribution of non-pivot columns.
conclusion: Exploiting the zeta-transform structure of the kernel computation gives a provable, exact speedup of the attack's dominant cost without altering the overall key-recovery algorithm, highlighting post-quantum cryptanalysis as a subject requiring further classical algorithmic work.

title: Compressibility Is Not Feedback: A Random-access Gap In Causal Semantic Repair
authors: Milad Bafarassat
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic feedback can repair a noisy first decode without retransmitting the whole message, but current end-to-end evaluations hide where a feedback design fails. An oracle that sees both the source-side state and receiver observation may describe a useful correction with few bits, while the receiver, which sees only its own observation, may not know which correction to request. We formulate these as distinct direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, connect repair distortion to retained local utility and prove a random-access separation: one direct bit is exact although receiver utility vanishes with the number of source-conditioned alternatives. A synthetic ladder verifies the exact law. In paired populations of eight Reuters text-JSCC codecs, the trained recurrent population retains over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than the trained DeepSC population despite comparable full-repair opportunity. Nevertheless, an entropy-valid receiver audit across all eight recurrent checkpoints does not resolve against repetition, source-only or shuffled-index controls. The results show that compressible repair is an upper bound, not evidence of deployable feedback, and motivate reporting both rate curves under matched resources.
tldr: The paper shows that compressible semantic repair is not equivalent to deployable feedback, proving a random-access gap between direct and receiver-constrained coding.
motivation: Semantic feedback can help repair noisy decodes without full retransmission, but current evaluations hide where a design fails because they ignore the receiver's constrained knowledge.
method: The authors formulate direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, prove a random-access separation, and test it with a synthetic ladder and paired populations of Reuters text-JSCC codecs including recurrent and DeepSC models.
result: One direct bit can be exact while receiver utility vanishes with source-conditioned alternatives; trained recurrent codecs retain over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than DeepSC, but an entropy-valid receiver audit does not resolve against controls.
conclusion: Compressible repair is an upper bound and not evidence of deployable feedback, motivating matched-resource reporting of both rate curves.

title: Fastar: Fri Accelerator For Scalable Transparent ARguments Of Knowledge
authors: Xiaolin Xu Tengkai Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) enable a prover to cryptographically convince a verifier of the validity of a statement without revealing any underlying secrets, forming a foundational primitive for verifiable computation. The ZKP landscape is undergoing a fundamental shift from classic zk-SNARKs such as Groth16, which rely on trusted setup and are vulnerable to quantum adversaries, toward transparent, post-quantum constructions such as zk-STARK. These systems achieve post-quantum security by relying solely on collision-resistant hash functions, however, at the cost of substantial computational overhead. In particular, the Fast Reed--Solomon Interactive Oracle Proof of Proximity (FRI) protocol dominates prover complexity, generating massive data volumes, repeated Merkle-tree commitments, and irregular memory access patterns that limit performance and energy efficiency on general-purpose processors. To address these challenges, this work proposes FASTAR, a novel FPGA-based accelerator for the FRI protocol. Unlike accelerators that pursue fixed high-performance kernels on expensive ASIC process nodes, FASTAR adopts a constraint-driven design methodology. Our framework is implemented with High-Level Synthesis (HLS) and composed of fully parameterizable building blocks for the major stages of FRI, including polynomial evaluation, recursive split-and-fold, and Merkle-tree construction. From user-provided board specifications, FASTAR automatically generates hardware implementations tailored to the resource and memory constraints of the target FPGA, enabling deployment across a wide range of platforms without manual redesign.
tldr: FASTAR is an FPGA-based accelerator for the FRI protocol that dominates prover cost in zk-STARK transparent post-quantum proof systems.
motivation: The shift from trusted-setup zk-SNARKs to transparent, post-quantum zk-STARKs comes at the cost of large prover overhead, with the FRI protocol generating massive data volumes, repeated Merkle-tree commitments, and irregular memory access patterns that limit efficiency on general-purpose processors.
method: The authors adopt a constraint-driven design methodology in High-Level Synthesis, building fully parameterizable hardware blocks covering polynomial evaluation, recursive split-and-fold, and Merkle-tree construction, then automatically generating implementations tailored to user-supplied FPGA board specifications.
result: The generated designs adapt to the resource and memory constraints of a wide range of target FPGAs without manual redesign, delivering accelerated FRI performance compared with general-purpose processors.
conclusion: FASTAR provides a portable, transparent-proof acceleration framework demonstrating that scalable zk-STARK proving can be efficiently mapped onto reconfigurable hardware.

title: On The OpenAI Whole-cube Bound
authors: Alex Samorodnitsky
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is an essentially derivative note, whose goal is to interpret the 'whole-cube' bound of OpenAI for binary codes in a possibly somewhat more accessible way. This is attained, in part, by connecting it to some previously known results. All of the heavy technical lifting in the interpretation below is also due to the OpenAI language models ChatGPT 5.6 and ChatGPT 6. With that, we hope that the statements of the main results, the ensuing discussion, and the arguments themselves may be of some interest.
tldr: A derivative note interpreting OpenAI's 'whole-cube' bound for binary codes in a more accessible way and connecting it to previously known results.
motivation: To make the whole-cube bound for binary codes more accessible by linking it to established coding-theoretic results.
method: Interpretation and exposition of the bound, with heavy technical work reportedly performed by OpenAI language models.
result: Provides an accessible interpretation of the bound and some connections to known results, but no new primary research results.
conclusion: The note may be of some interest as an exposition, but it is derivative and classical, with no direct relevance to quantum information theory.

title: Momentum-Space Planar Optics For Long-Range Spin Hamiltonians
authors: Huaqiang Li, Junxu Liu, Guangfeng Wang, Erez Hasman, Xianfeng Chen, Bo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating spin Hamiltonians with dense, long-range interactions requires repeated global summation over many pairwise couplings, making energy evaluation costly on conventional electronic hardware. Here, we realize a planar optical architecture that evaluates such interaction energies directly in momentum space. For translationally structured couplings, the interaction kernel is encoded in the spatial transmission of a subwavelength-thick planar optical element placed in the Fourier plane. Pointwise spectral weighting followed by total-power detection reduces the quadratic spin Hamiltonian to a single optical signal, avoiding repeated digital multiply-accumulate operations during energy evaluation. We experimentally apply this approach to frustrated finite-range models and fully connected spin systems with oscillatory long-range couplings. The measured energies agree closely with numerical calculations, while optical annealing reproduces low-energy configurations and landscape statistics, reaching a normalized solution quality of 99.9%. These results establish momentum-space planar optics as a compact physical computing primitive for global-interaction problems in statistical physics and optimization.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a subwavelength-thick planar optical element that evaluates long-range spin-Hamiltonian interaction energies in the Fourier (momentum) plane, achieving 99.9% normalized solution quality on frustrated and fully connected spin models.
motivation: Evaluating dense, long-range spin Hamiltonians requires costly repeated global summations over pairwise couplings on conventional digital hardware, motivating a physical computing primitive that performs these quadratic energy evaluations in a single optical step.
method: The interaction kernel of translationally structured couplings is encoded in the spatial transmission of a planar optical element placed in the Fourier plane, so that pointwise spectral weighting followed by total-power detection yields the full quadratic spin energy without digital multiply-accumulate operations; the scheme is tested experimentally on frustrated finite-range and fully connected oscillatory-coupling models.
result: Measured energies agree closely with numerical calculations, and optical annealing reproduces low-energy configurations and landscape statistics with a normalized solution quality of 99.9%.
conclusion: Momentum-space planar optics is proposed as a compact physical computing primitive for global-interaction problems in statistical physics and optimization.

title: Comparing The Lee-Yang Gap With The Mass Gap In The Sub-critical Planar Ising Model
authors: Noam Borgnia, Jui-Hui Chung, Jacob Shapiro
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the subcritical mass gap is comparable to the Lee-Yang gap over free-boundary square boxes raised to the power [MATH]. Random-current moment bounds, a correlation inequality and a finite block expansion give the upper bound. The lower bound follows from the Lee-Yang product, the susceptibility and the critical magnetization. We also obtain uniform factorial bounds on the field derivatives of the pressure.
tldr: The paper proves that in the subcritical planar Ising model the mass gap is comparable to the Lee-Yang gap on free-boundary square boxes, up to a power-law factor.
motivation: The relationship between the Lee-Yang edge singularity and the mass gap is a fundamental question in rigorous statistical mechanics, connecting analytic structure of the pressure to correlation decay.
method: The authors use random-current moment bounds, a correlation inequality, and a finite block expansion for the upper bound, and the Lee-Yang product together with susceptibility and critical magnetization for the lower bound.
result: They establish comparability of the subcritical mass gap and the Lee-Yang gap on square boxes raised to a power, and also derive uniform factorial bounds on the field derivatives of the pressure.
conclusion: The work rigorously links the Lee-Yang gap to the mass gap in the subcritical planar Ising model, extending control over analytic and correlation properties of the model.

title: The Isac Tradeoff Cliff: Fundamental Limits Under Waveform Uncertainty And Finite Blocklength
authors: Lajos Hanzo Mohammed Zafar Ali Khan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) enables the joint design of communication and sensing functionalities using a shared waveform, but its performance critically depends on the accuracy of the transmitted signal available at the sensing receiver. In practical systems, this signal is obtained by finite blocklength decoding . This paper develops an analytical framework for quantifying the impact of the associated decoding uncertainty on sensing performance. We model decoding errors via an equivalent noise formulation that captures their second-order effect on the sensing receiver, and derive the corresponding Fisher Information and Cram\'er--Rao Bound (CRB). The resultant characterization reveals a fundamental sensing--communication tradeoff governed by the communication rate and decoding reliability. This shows that the classical finite blocklength reliability results in a fundamentally new insight concerning ISAC systems: when the decoded communication waveforms are reused as sensing references in a data-aided fashion, the communication reliability boundary also acts as a sensing-information bound. {We identify and characterize a sharp transition in sensing performance -- referred to as the Tradeoff Cliff -- arising from finite blocklength reliability effects.} This transition separates the regimes of near-ideal sensing performance from those of excessive estimation error as the communication rate approaches capacity. Furthermore, we provide an explicit expression for the critical rate at which this transition occurs, showing its dependence on blocklength, channel dispersion, and target error probability. Monte Carlo simulations under both AWGN and block fading channels validate the theoretical analysis and confirm the trend observed. The results provide design insights for operating ISAC systems with an appropriate reliability margin to avoid severe sensing degradation.
tldr: This paper derives Fisher information and Cramér–Rao bounds for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) under finite-blocklength decoding uncertainty, revealing a sharp 'Tradeoff Cliff' in sensing performance as the communication rate approaches capacity.
motivation: ISAC systems reuse the decoded communication waveform as a sensing reference, so finite-blocklength decoding errors degrade sensing accuracy; the authors aim to quantify this coupled reliability–sensing limit.
method: Decoding errors are modeled as an equivalent second-order noise source on the sensing receiver, from which the Fisher Information and Cramér–Rao Bound are derived analytically, with Monte Carlo validation under AWGN and block fading channels.
result: The analysis yields a fundamental sensing–communication tradeoff, an explicit critical-rate expression (depending on blocklength, channel dispersion, and target error probability) marking the 'Tradeoff Cliff' between near-ideal and excessive estimation error.
conclusion: The finite-blocklength reliability boundary also acts as a sensing-information bound, providing design guidance on reliability margins to avoid severe sensing degradation in ISAC systems.

title: Code Equivalence And Automorphism Problems For Codes
authors: Jean-Francois Biasse, Alexandra V. Hostetler, Anuvrat Jaindungarwal
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the complexity of the Code Equivalence problem and show that it is polynomially equivalent to several computational automorphism problems for codes. These problems ask for the cardinality (ACOUNT), an orbit partition (APART), and a generating set (AGEN) for the permutation automorphism group of a code. We present deterministic, polynomial-time reductions between Permutation Code Equivalence (PCE) and each of these problems, including a one-shot reduction from search-PCE to AGEN that makes a single oracle call. We present similar reductions between Linear Code Equivalence (LCE) and analogous problems for the monomial automorphism group of a code. All of our reductions work for any linear codes.
tldr: This paper shows that the Code Equivalence problem is polynomially equivalent to several automorphism problems for classical linear codes.
motivation: Code equivalence and automorphism are central computational problems in classical coding theory, with cryptographic relevance, but their interrelationships are not fully understood.
method: The authors give deterministic polynomial-time reductions between Permutation Code Equivalence (PCE) and ACOUNT, APART, and AGEN for permutation automorphism groups, and analogous reductions for Linear Code Equivalence (LCE) and monomial automorphism groups.
result: They establish polynomial equivalence, including a one-shot reduction from search-PCE to AGEN requiring a single oracle call, for arbitrary linear codes.
conclusion: The work clarifies complexity relationships among classical code equivalence and automorphism problems, but does not involve quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Haagerup-Izumi Fusion Categories
authors: Terry Gannon, Andrew Schopieray, Harshit Yadav
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every odd [MATH], we construct a Haagerup-Izumi (HI) category for [MATH], using Barnes double-sine functions. Equivariantization gives near-group categories of type [MATH] for every odd [MATH]. We classify connected separable algebras up to Morita equivalence in such HI categories and describe their dual categories. These duals are often HI for noncyclic groups with nontrivial pointed associators. We prove the Evans-Gannon conjecture that the modular data of the center is always a smashed sum involving a finite metric group of order [MATH] and recover this group and its quadratic form directly from the data of the HI category. We also give the HI equations and reconstruction in arbitrary characteristic and prove a Frobenius symmetry in characteristic two. Using this, we obtain the complete list of (untwisted, subfactor type) HI categories over [MATH] for odd [MATH]. Other applications include finding three pairwise non-Morita-equivalent [MATH] categories whose centers have the same modular data. We show that the center of a [MATH] HI category cannot be defined (i.e., admits no split ribbon form) over a cyclotomic field, disproving a conjecture of Davidovich-Hagge-Wang.
tldr: The paper constructs and classifies Haagerup-Izumi fusion categories using Barnes double-sine functions, proving structural results and a conjecture about their modular data.
motivation: Haagerup-Izumi categories are a class of fusion categories arising in subfactor theory, and their classification and modular data are of interest in pure mathematics and mathematical physics.
method: The authors use Barnes double-sine functions to construct HI categories, apply equivariantization to obtain near-group categories, and classify connected separable algebras up to Morita equivalence to describe dual categories.
result: They prove the Evans-Gannon conjecture that the center's modular data is a smashed sum over a finite metric group, recover the group and quadratic form from HI data, and obtain a complete list of untwisted subfactor-type HI categories over C for odd indices.
conclusion: The work resolves several conjectures and provides new classification results in fusion category theory, but its content is purely mathematical and not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: The Use Of Coherent States In The Excitation And Ionization Of Atoms By A Short Symmetric Pulse
authors: Jorge E. Miraglia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new model for describing the excitation of atoms by short symmetric pulses. The theory is based on the impulse approximation and incorporates a confining potential approximated by a harmonic oscillator. Results are presented for a wide variety of parameters, including field intensity and laser frequency. Permitted and forbidden transitions are analyzed in detail. The photon energy spectrum presents peaks attributed to multiphoton absorption. Our model demonstrates robustness and reliability, paving the way for addressing more complex scenarios.
tldr: The paper proposes a model for atomic excitation and ionization by short symmetric pulses using coherent states, the impulse approximation, and a harmonic oscillator confining potential.
motivation: The authors aim to describe atomic excitation by short symmetric laser pulses and analyze permitted transitions, multiphoton absorption peaks, and dependence on field intensity and frequency.
method: The theory is based on the impulse approximation combined with a harmonic oscillator approximation for the confining potential, using coherent states to model the atom-field interaction.
result: The model produces photon energy spectra with peaks attributed to multiphoton absorption, and it is shown to be robust across a wide range of field intensities and laser frequencies, with forbidden and permitted transitions analyzed in detail.
conclusion: The work provides a reliable framework for describing short-pulse atomic excitation and ionization, potentially extensible to more complex scenarios.

title: Spin-multiplexed Terahertz Image Edge Detection Based On Extrinsic Chirality In All-dielectric Metasurface
authors: Yuxin Tang, Shichao Zhao, Li Luo, Tingting Tang, Hang Xu, Jie Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extrinsically chiral metasurfaces can exhibit pronounced chiral responses in planar structures without intrinsic chirality, making them attractive for spin-selective light manipulation. Here, we propose a transmissive all-dielectric terahertz metasurface for image edge detection. Owing to the extrinsic chiral response, the metasurface enables edge-enhanced imaging under right-handed circularly polarized incidence near 0.69 THz, while preserving bright-field imaging under left-handed circularly polarized incidence. Spatial-frequency analysis shows that the effective numerical aperture of the device is approximately 0.4, indicating the terahertz image edge detection can be achieved over a broad spatial-frequency range. This work provides a new design route toward transmissive terahertz all-optical image processing with spin selectivity and a large numerical aperture.
tldr: A transmissive all-dielectric terahertz metasurface exploiting extrinsic chirality performs spin-selective image edge detection with a numerical aperture of ~0.4 at 0.69 THz.
motivation: Extrinsically chiral planar metasurfaces offer strong chiral responses without intrinsic chirality, making them attractive for spin-selective optical manipulation and compact all-optical image processing at terahertz frequencies.
method: The authors design and simulate a transmissive all-dielectric terahertz metasurface whose extrinsic chiral response enables edge-enhanced imaging under right-handed circularly polarized incidence while retaining bright-field imaging under left-handed circular polarization, characterized via spatial-frequency analysis.
result: Edge-enhanced imaging is demonstrated near 0.69 THz under RCP incidence with an effective numerical aperture of approximately 0.4, supporting edge detection over a broad spatial-frequency range.
conclusion: The work offers a new design route for transmissive terahertz all-optical image processing with spin selectivity and a large numerical aperture, though it is a classical photonic device result with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: Asymptotics For Partition Functions Of Random Normal Matrix Models With Singularities
authors: Kohei Noda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study determinantal planar Coulomb gases with a smooth radial potential, a smooth radial perturbation, jump-type singularities (including the bulk, semi-hard, hard, and soft-edge regimes), and a hard wall region given by a centered disk, a disk complement, or an annulus. We obtain explicit asymptotic expansions of the partition functions up to and including the term of order [MATH]. Our results unify and generalize many of the earlier works.
tldr: This paper derives explicit asymptotic expansions for partition functions of random normal matrix models with various singularities and hard-wall geometries.
motivation: Random normal matrix models and planar Coulomb gases are central in mathematical physics, but their partition function asymptotics with singularities and hard walls remain incompletely unified.
method: The author studies determinantal planar Coulomb gases with smooth radial potentials, perturbations, jump-type singularities, and hard-wall regions, using asymptotic analysis to obtain expansions up to a specified order.
result: Explicit asymptotic expansions of the partition functions are obtained for bulk, semi-hard, hard, and soft-edge singularity regimes, unifying and generalizing many earlier works.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive asymptotic framework for partition functions of random normal matrix models with singularities and hard-wall constraints.

title: Lee-Huang-Yang Energy For Dilute Bose Gases: An Upper Bound For General Potentials
authors: Giulia Basti, Morris Brooks, Serena Cenatiempo, Alessandro Olgiati, Benjamin Schlein
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an upper bound for the ground state energy density of a dilute Bose gas, interacting through a general short-range, repulsive potential. To reach this goal, we extend the approach recently introduced in [1] for hard spheres.
tldr: The paper proves an upper bound for the Lee-Huang-Yang ground-state energy density of a dilute Bose gas with general short-range repulsive potentials.
motivation: Extending energy bounds beyond the hard-sphere case is important for understanding dilute Bose gases with more realistic interactions.
method: The authors generalize a recent approach for hard spheres to arbitrary short-range repulsive potentials, using rigorous many-body techniques.
result: An upper bound for the ground-state energy density is established for general short-range repulsive potentials.
conclusion: The work advances the mathematical physics of dilute Bose gases but is not aligned with quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Topological Edge States Enable Step-like Power Transfer For Robust Arbitrary-Ratio Power Splitting
authors: Jihwan You, Jibaek Song, Seungyong Lee, Sangsik Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological edge states offer a robust route to photonic devices and systems that remain functional despite structural imperfections. Topological waveguide arrays have been shown to deliver robust coupling, but only for full power transfer between the two edge waveguides---a robust route to an arbitrary intermediate ratio has remained unknown. Here we show that the topological edge states of a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, realized with only four identical waveguides, form an arbitrary-ratio power splitter whose ratio is robust to both the device length and fabrication errors. Two near-degenerate edge supermodes beat to produce a step-like power transfer with a flat, length-insensitive plateau, in contrast to the sinusoidal transfer of a conventional directional coupler. The splitting ratio at this plateau is governed by the difference between the two waveguide gaps, making it immune to correlated fabrication offsets. We derive this behavior analytically and confirm it numerically and experimentally on a conventional silicon-on-insulator platform. Beyond this device, our analysis can be applied to general topological waveguide arrays, while the robust splitter offers a practical building block for fabrication-tolerant photonic circuits.
tldr: A four-waveguide Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topological photonic chain realizes a length- and fabrication-robust arbitrary-ratio power splitter via beating of near-degenerate edge supermodes.
motivation: Topological waveguide arrays previously allowed only full power transfer between edge waveguides, leaving robust arbitrary-ratio splitting unrealized despite its value for fabrication-tolerant photonic circuits.
method: The authors analytically derive the beating dynamics of two near-degenerate topological edge supermodes in a finite SSH chain, then verify the predicted step-like power transfer numerically and experimentally on a silicon-on-insulator platform.
result: The splitter exhibits a flat, length-insensitive plateau in transferred power whose ratio is set by the difference between the two waveguide gaps, making it immune to correlated fabrication offsets.
conclusion: The demonstrated device provides a practical, robust building block for photonic circuits and the analysis generalizes to other topological waveguide arrays.

title: Finite Rodriguez-Villegas Approximants To The Riemann $\xi$-Function
authors: Alisson M. Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a sequence of finite Rodriguez-Villegas transforms converging locally uniformly to the Riemann [MATH]-function in the critical strip. The input is a positive symmetric profile on the unit interval obtained from the Riemann theta kernel through convolution with the hyperbolic-secant kernel and the logistic coordinate. The profile is a Stieltjes function of [MATH]. Its Bernstein polynomials produce reciprocal numerators and exact finite functional equations. The same numerators admit an exact realization as fermionic supertraces, while the Bernstein polynomials are normalized Gibbs traces.
tldr: The paper constructs finite Rodriguez-Villegas transforms that converge locally uniformly to the Riemann xi-function in the critical strip.
motivation: The work aims to provide finite approximants to the Riemann xi-function and uncover exact algebraic and statistical structures underlying its analytic behavior.
method: It uses a positive symmetric profile derived from the Riemann theta kernel via convolution with a hyperbolic-secant kernel and logistic coordinate, then studies its Bernstein polynomials and reciprocal numerators.
result: The construction yields exact finite functional equations, a realization of the numerators as fermionic supertraces, and an interpretation of the Bernstein polynomials as normalized Gibbs traces.
conclusion: The paper offers a novel number-theoretic approximation scheme linking the Riemann xi-function to combinatorial and statistical-mechanical objects, though it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Photonic Half-semimetals With Dual Semimetal-insulator Topology
authors: Zi-Xuan Gao, Xiaohan Cui, Xiao-Dong Chen, Ke-Yi Zeng, Hao-Chang Mo, Xin-Tao He, Ruo-Yang Zhang, C. T. Chan, Jian-Wen Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.
tldr: The paper demonstrates photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology enabling spin-valley-locked beam splitting and multilane helical transport.
motivation: Topological semimetals lack intrinsic channel selectivity while topological insulators confine transport to narrow interfaces, motivating a dual-topology platform that combines bulk transport with selective routing.
method: Time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals are theoretically designed and experimentally realized, with selective bandgap closing in spin-valley space and superlattice assembly.
result: The half-semimetal acts as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, and a superlattice of four complementary HSMs enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization.
conclusion: Photonic half-semimetals establish a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

title: On Disjointness And $\mathscr{F}$-product Recurrence With Respect To Zero Entropy Systems
authors: Xinxing Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies disjointness and \(\)-product recurrence with respect to zero-entropy systems. First, we prove that, for a point whose orbit closure has zero topological entropy, \[ \rightleftharpoons \Finf\PRzero\rightleftharpoons \Fpubd\PRzero \rightleftharpoons \Fps\PRzero \rightovernotleft \Fs\PRzero. \] We also construct a minimal topological dynamical system with uniform positive entropy which is disjoint from all zero-entropy \(M\)-systems but is not disjoint from some zero-entropy \(E\)-system, i.e., \(\Ezero^{\perp}\subsetneq \Mzero^{\perp}\), giving an affirmative answer to a question of \cite[W.~Huang, K.~K. Park and X.~Ye, Topological disjointness from entropy zero systems, Bull. Soc. Math. France (2007), 259--282]. Moreover, the same construction shows that there exists an \(\Fps\PRzero\) point which is not \(\Fpubd\PRzero\), i.e., [MATH] [MATH], giving a negative answer to a question of \cite[P.~Oprocha and G.~H. Zhang, On weak product recurrence and synchronization of return times, Adv. Math. (2013), 395--412].
tldr: This paper studies disjointness and F-product recurrence properties of zero-entropy topological dynamical systems, answering two open questions in topological dynamics.
motivation: The work aims to characterize which systems are disjoint from all zero-entropy systems and to clarify the relationships between different notions of product recurrence for points with zero-entropy orbit closures.
method: The author employs constructions of minimal topological dynamical systems with uniform positive entropy and analyzes orbit closures with zero topological entropy, deriving a hierarchy of recurrence conditions and separating various classes via explicit counterexamples.
result: It is shown that E^⊥_0 is a strict subset of M^⊥_0 (a minimal UPE system disjoint from all zero-entropy M-systems but not from some zero-entropy E-system), and that an F-ps recurrence point need not be F-pubd recurrence.
conclusion: The results resolve questions of Huang-Park-Ye and Oprocha-Zhang, deepening the understanding of disjointness from zero-entropy systems and product recurrence in topological dynamics.

title: Subspace Coverings And Generalized Covering Radii Of Generalized Zetterberg Codes
authors: Shitao Li, Yang Li, Gaojun Luo, Zhonghua Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized covering radii measure how many columns of a parity-check matrix are needed to generate several syndromes simultaneously. Their finite-geometric counterparts are [MATH]-saturating sets, for which every [MATH]-dimensional subspace is contained in a subspace generated by at most [MATH] prescribed vectors. We investigate this covering problem for the norm-one configurations associated with generalized Zetterberg codes. We establish the upper bound [MATH] over every nonbinary finite field and in an explicit binary range, together with complementary lower bounds obtained by counting subspaces and constructing subfield obstructions. For an explicit range of large [MATH], these configurations are [MATH]-strong blocking sets, and the [MATH] generalized covering radius attains its minimum possible value [MATH]. For binary Zetterberg codes, we determine the second generalized covering radius in every extension degree and prove that the third radius is seven for an infinite subfamily.
tldr: The paper studies subspace coverings and generalized covering radii of generalized Zetterberg codes using finite-geometric saturating sets and blocking sets.
motivation: Generalized covering radii arise in coding theory and finite geometry, but the specific problem for generalized Zetterberg codes is not connected to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze norm-one configurations associated with generalized Zetterberg codes, establish upper bounds over nonbinary finite fields and a binary range, and derive lower bounds by counting subspaces and constructing subfield obstructions.
result: They prove upper bounds on generalized covering radii, identify ranges where the configurations are strong blocking sets attaining minimal radius, and determine the second and third generalized covering radii for binary Zetterberg codes in specific cases.
conclusion: The work advances classical coding theory and finite geometry but has no clear relevance to the user's quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems interests.

title: Akapinn: Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Physics-Informed Neural Networks For Approximating Solutions To Quasilinear Partial Differential Equations
authors: B. Veena S. N. Rao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A controlled comparative study of a mesh-free Kolmogorov--Arnold Physics-Informed Neural Network (KAN-PINN) applied to nonlinear strain-limiting partial differential equations is presented. Three distinct training runs across varying material-parameter pairs [MATH] are evaluated within a fixed computational pipeline comprising an exact hard boundary ansatz, a robust pseudo-Huber residual loss, and a multi-stage Adam-to-L-BFGS optimizer schedule. A fundamental metric inversion is revealed by the analysis: while training loss reflects operator-specific residual scaling and constitutive stiffness, the operator-independent relative [MATH] error demonstrates that intermediate parameter regimes achieve superior solution accuracy and enhanced generalization.
tldr: The paper introduces Akapinn, an adaptive Kolmogorov–Arnold Physics-Informed Neural Network for approximating solutions to nonlinear strain-limiting quasilinear PDEs, compared across three material-parameter regimes.
motivation: Mesh-free neural solvers such as PINNs offer a route to solving nonlinear PDEs without discretization, and the authors aim to characterize how parameter-dependent constitutive stiffness affects training and solution accuracy.
method: KAN-PINN architectures are trained in a fixed pipeline that combines an exact hard boundary ansatz, a pseudo-Huber residual loss, and a multi-stage Adam-to-L-BFGS schedule, evaluated over three runs with varying material-parameter pairs.
result: Training loss scales with operator-specific residual magnitude and constitutive stiffness, but the operator-independent relative L2 error reveals that intermediate parameter regimes yield the best solution accuracy and generalization.
conclusion: The study highlights a metric inversion between loss and true error, suggesting intermediate material-parameter regimes are preferable, though no quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid-system content is involved.

title: Order Automorphisms Of Partial Isometries In $M_n(\mathbb C)$
authors: Guoxing Ji Fengyang Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate and characterize order automorphisms on the set of partial isometries in the finite-dimensional matrix algebra [MATH]. Different from the classical order automorphisms of subspace lattices, which can be implemented by standard invertible or unitary transformations, the order automorphisms considered herein admit no such conventional matrix representations. Instead, they are essentially governed by matrices such that [MATH] is either positive or negative invertible. The results reveal that the structural features of order automorphisms for partial isometries are substantially more intricate than those of classical subspace automorphisms.
tldr: The paper characterizes order automorphisms on the set of partial isometries in finite-dimensional matrix algebras, showing they are governed by positive or negative invertible matrices rather than standard unitary transformations.
motivation: Order automorphisms of subspace lattices are classically implemented by invertible or unitary transformations, but the analogous problem for partial isometries is structurally different and remains to be understood.
method: The authors analyze order-theoretic automorphisms acting on partial isometries in M_n(C) and derive their matrix representations via positivity or negativity of associated invertible matrices.
result: Order automorphisms for partial isometries admit no conventional matrix representations; instead, they are essentially determined by matrices whose entries are either positive or negative invertible.
conclusion: The structure of order automorphisms for partial isometries is substantially more intricate than that of classical subspace automorphisms, revealing new operator-algebraic phenomena.

title: Nonlinear Thermodynamic Formalism For Correspondences
authors: Dingxuan Tang, Rui Yang, Zhiming Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a nonlinear thermodynamic formalism for correspondences on compact metric spaces. A continuous energy is evaluated on empirical measures of successive pairs of states. The measure-theoretic pressure of a stationary transition pair is the sum of its kernel entropy and the energy of the joint distribution of two successive states. For forward expansive correspondences satisfying an ergodic-abundance condition, we prove a variational principle and the existence of nonlinear equilibrium pairs. We further prove that limits of the two-coordinate projections of asymptotically maximizing Gibbs ensembles are averages of the two-coordinate distributions of equilibrium pairs. When the energy depends on finitely many potentials on the space of admissible pairs, Legendre regularity assumptions allow us to identify nonlinear equilibrium pairs among linear equilibrium pairs through a self-consistency equation and a global maximization condition. Under these assumptions, real analyticity in one dimension and uniqueness of linear equilibrium pairs imply finiteness of the nonlinear equilibrium set. Finite-state examples exhibit continuous and first-order transitions, metastability, and phases that have identical one-coordinate marginals but distinct two-coordinate distributions. A criterion based on Taylor expansions determines the associated critical exponents.
tldr: The paper develops a nonlinear thermodynamic formalism for correspondences on compact metric spaces, establishing variational principles and equilibrium pairs.
motivation: The work extends thermodynamic formalism from single maps to correspondences, motivated by a desire to understand measure-theoretic pressure and equilibrium states for multi-valued dynamics.
method: It defines pressure via kernel entropy and energy on joint distributions, proves a variational principle for forward expansive correspondences under an ergodic-abundance condition, and analyzes Gibbs ensembles and Legendre regularity.
result: Key results include existence of nonlinear equilibrium pairs, characterization via self-consistency and global maximization, finiteness under analyticity and uniqueness assumptions, and examples with phase transitions and metastability.
conclusion: The formalism captures novel two-coordinate phenomena and critical exponents, offering a mathematical framework for nonlinear thermodynamic behavior in dynamical systems.

title: Arithmetic $k$-Polynomial Dynamical Localization For $k$ Power-Law Quasi-Periodic Long-Range Operators On $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$
authors: Ao Cai, Huihui Lv, Yuan Shan, Xueyin Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a criterion of arithmetic [MATH]-polynomial spectral localization and [MATH]-polynomial dynamical localization in expectation for quasi-periodic long-range operators on [MATH] with power-law hopping based on the quantitative [MATH]-reducibility of the dual Schr\"odinger cocycle. As the application, we prove both localization properties for power-law long-range perturbations of the Almost Mathieu Operators with sufficiently large couplings and Diophantine frequencies.
tldr: The paper proves arithmetic k-polynomial spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic long-range operators with power-law hopping on l^2(Z^d).
motivation: The authors aim to extend localization results to long-range quasi-periodic operators using quantitative reducibility of the dual Schrödinger cocycle.
method: They establish a criterion based on quantitative reducibility of the dual cocycle and apply it to power-law long-range perturbations of Almost Mathieu Operators.
result: They obtain both spectral and dynamical localization in expectation for sufficiently large couplings and Diophantine frequencies.
conclusion: The work provides a general criterion for arithmetic polynomial localization in long-range quasi-periodic systems, with Almost Mathieu operators as a key application.

title: Not All 4-bit Quantizers Are Equal: Deployment-Time Mitigation Of Pii Leakage In Fine-Tuned Small Language Models
authors: Diego Kreutz Cristhian Kapelinski
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organizations fine-tune small language models on private data and then compress them to 4 bits for resource-efficient deployment. We show that the compression method also affects privacy. What separates the methods is not the bit width but whether they tune their rounding on a small sample of text, the calibration corpus. On our primary model, when each planted record's own opening text is used as the prompt, the two calibration-based methods we test, Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) and Gradient-based Post-Training Quantization (GPTQ), each reproduce none of the planted records, while the calibration-corpus-free GGUF Q4_K_M format reproduces 5.3% of them. Tracked across five open models with 0.5-7 billion parameters, AWQ leaks least at every size and in both families, with little accuracy loss at 3-7 billion. Controlled experiments associate the difference with calibration-induced rounding error in channels involved in rare-token prediction. Choosing the 4-bit method is therefore a deployment-time privacy decision, not only a question of speed and quality.
tldr: The paper shows that the choice of 4-bit quantization method affects privacy leakage in fine-tuned small language models, with calibration-based methods like AWQ leaking less than GGUF Q4_K_M.
motivation: Organizations compress private fine-tuned models to 4 bits for deployment, but the privacy implications of different quantization methods are not well understood.
method: The authors compare AWQ, GPTQ, and GGUF Q4_K_M across five open models (0.5–7B parameters), measuring reproduction of planted private records and relating leakage to calibration-induced rounding error.
result: Calibration-based methods reproduced none of the planted records in the primary setting, while calibration-free GGUF Q4_K_M reproduced 5.3%; AWQ leaked least across sizes and families with minimal accuracy loss at 3–7B.
conclusion: Selecting a 4-bit quantization method is a deployment-time privacy decision, not merely a speed/quality trade-off.

title: Pushout Attachments And Conditional Complexity Of Executable Models
authors: Alexander Kolpakov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We represent the modular enlargement of an executable model by a pushout of finite typed presentations. Adhesivity preserves the original model and recovers the shared interface, while chosen pushouts make linking functorial and coproducts describe parallel attachments. A semantic comparison gives a precise criterion for behavioral persistence. Effective linking also bounds conditional prefix complexity; under the stated canonicalization and invariance assumptions, attachment and extension codes yield the same profiles of loss against complexity, up to additive constants, and share an exact scalar envelope. The result separates syntax, semantics, ideal complexity, and concrete coding cost, and shows that a preference for modularity can arise only through restrictions on the permitted attachments.
tldr: The paper uses pushouts of finite typed presentations to model modular enlargement of executable models and analyzes conditional prefix complexity of attachment and extension codes.
motivation: The work aims to give a categorical account of linking modular executable models and to study how behavioral persistence and coding complexity depend on attachment choices.
method: It represents modular enlargement via pushouts, proves adhesivity and functoriality of chosen pushouts, and derives bounds on conditional prefix complexity under canonicalization and invariance assumptions.
result: Attachment and extension codes yield the same loss-vs-complexity profiles up to additive constants and share an exact scalar envelope, separating syntax, semantics, ideal complexity, and concrete coding cost.
conclusion: A preference for modularity can arise only through restrictions on permitted attachments, linking category-theoretic model composition to algorithmic information costs.

title: Improved Algorithms For The Remote Point Problem
authors: Ben Lee Volk
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Remote Point Problem (RPP) is an algorithmic problem that asks, given a linear subspace [MATH] of dimension [MATH], to deterministically find a vector [MATH] far in Hamming distance from [MATH]. This problem was introduced by Alon, Panigrahy and Yekhanin [APY09], motivated in part by the matrix rigidity approach for proving circuit lower bounds. An algorithm is said to achieve remoteness [MATH] if it finds a vector [MATH] whose Hamming distance from [MATH] is at least [MATH]. We observe that over the rational numbers, the problem admits a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that achieves optimal remoteness [MATH]. Over finite fields, we obtain a (modest) improvement of a result of Alon, Panigrahy and Yekhanin [APY09], and give an algorithm that achieves remoteness [MATH].
tldr: The paper improves deterministic algorithms for the Remote Point Problem, which finds a vector far in Hamming distance from a given linear subspace.
motivation: The Remote Point Problem was introduced partly to support the matrix rigidity approach for proving circuit lower bounds. Better algorithms may strengthen this line of attack.
method: The author gives deterministic polynomial-time algorithms, achieving optimal remoteness over the rationals and a modest improvement over previous results over finite fields.
result: Over rational numbers, the algorithm attains optimal remoteness; over finite fields, it improves the remoteness bound of Alon, Panigrahy, and Yekhanin [APY09].
conclusion: The work advances the algorithmic understanding of the Remote Point Problem, with potential implications for circuit lower bounds, but is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information.

title: Order-parameter-dependent Mobility In The Convective-Viscous Cahn-Hilliard Equation
authors: P. O. Mchedlov-Petrosyan, L. N. Davydov, O. A. Osmaev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generally the mobility in the Cahn-Hilliard equation may depend on the order parameter; this was evident already from the original derivation. However, explicit introduction of such dependence results in tremendous calculation difficulties, so the constant mobility approximation was commonly used. On the other hand, in several cases this dependence appeared to be crucial, so more realistic expressions were applied, usually positive powers or polynomials; still, for such dependencies only approximate and/or numerical solution exist. We consider 'reciprocal' linear and quadratic dependencies of mobility on the order parameter; for these dependencies exact traveling wave solutions are obtained. Even more, in a limited interval of the parameters reciprocal quadratic mobilities are rather good approximations to polynomial mobilities.
tldr: The paper derives exact traveling wave solutions for the convective-viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation with reciprocal linear and quadratic mobility dependencies on the order parameter.
motivation: Mobility in the Cahn-Hilliard equation can depend on the order parameter, but explicit dependencies usually make calculations intractable, so constant or polynomial approximations are common.
method: The authors introduce reciprocal linear and quadratic forms for the order-parameter-dependent mobility and solve the convective-viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation analytically for traveling wave solutions.
result: Exact traveling wave solutions are obtained, and over a limited parameter range the reciprocal quadratic mobility provides a good approximation to polynomial mobility forms.
conclusion: Reciprocal mobility dependencies offer an analytically tractable route to more realistic Cahn-Hilliard modeling, with potential use as approximations to polynomial mobilities.

title: On Soliton Asymptotics For Maxwell--Lorentz Equations With Rotating Particle
authors: Elena Kopylova
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 2D Maxwell--Lorentz equations with an extended charged rotating particle. The system admits soliton solutions corresponding to a particle moving with a constant velocity and rotating with a constant angular velocity. Our main result is the asymptotic stability of the solitons.
tldr: The paper proves asymptotic stability of soliton solutions for the 2D Maxwell–Lorentz equations with an extended charged rotating particle.
motivation: The Maxwell–Lorentz system describes a charged particle coupled to its own electromagnetic field, and understanding the stability of its soliton solutions is important for the mathematical theory of such systems.
method: The analysis uses PDE techniques, spectral analysis, and asymptotic stability estimates for soliton solutions in the rotating-particle setting.
result: The main result is the asymptotic stability of solitons corresponding to a particle moving with constant velocity and rotating with constant angular velocity.
conclusion: This work advances the mathematical study of soliton dynamics in classical electrodynamics but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Learning Continuous Reaction Paths For Transition-state Prediction
authors: Linlin Zhong Yexiang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transition states are defined by reaction pathways, yet most machine-learning methods predict them as isolated geometries. We introduce MARC-TS, a two-stage framework that learns a continuous, endpoint-conditioned path, queries it at any resolution and uses local path context to refine a transition-state candidate. We construct T1x-IRC-8K, a dataset of 8,209 reactions and 1,088,725 path-resolved geometries. On held-out reactions, the path model reduced complete-path error by 48.4% relative to endpoint interpolation, and the localizer achieved a mean aligned structural error of 0.127 {\AA}. Quantum-chemical optimization and vibrational analysis yielded 405 frequency-confirmed first-order saddle-point candidates from 410 predictions. In a 100-reaction nudged elastic band comparison, learned-path initialization reached a joint geometry-and-force target for 66% of reactions, compared with 12% for geometric interpolation after 100 optimizer steps. By treating the path as a reusable representation rather than an auxiliary output, MARC-TS connects transition-state prediction, mechanistic interpretation and quantum-chemical refinement.
tldr: MARC-TS learns continuous reaction paths to improve transition-state prediction and refinement.
motivation: Most machine-learning methods predict transition states as isolated geometries, ignoring the defining reaction pathway context.
method: A two-stage framework learns an endpoint-conditioned continuous path and uses local path context to refine a transition-state candidate, trained on a new 8,209-reaction dataset.
result: The path model reduced complete-path error by 48.4% over interpolation and achieved 0.127 Å mean aligned structural error; learned-path initialization reached joint geometry-and-force targets for 66% of reactions in a 100-reaction NEB comparison.
conclusion: Treating the path as a reusable representation connects transition-state prediction, mechanistic interpretation, and quantum-chemical refinement.

title: From Foundations To Applications: Reverse Mathematics And Philosophy
authors: Benedict Eastaugh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reverse mathematics is a branch of mathematical logic dedicated to determining the minimal set existence principles necessary and sufficient to derive ordinary mathematical theorems about concrete structures like the real line. Since the mid-1970s, reverse mathematics has developed a systematic classification of the strength of theorems in areas of mathematics ranging from real and complex analysis to infinitary combinatorics. This essay will place reverse mathematics in its historical and philosophical context, and reveal its relevance to central issues in the philosophy of mathematics, from the foundational programmes of Hilbert and Brouwer to contemporary debates about realism, determinacy, and applicability of mathematics. In doing so, it will discuss the role of computability theory in measuring the strength of set existence principles, as well as related questions about idealisation when these principles are applied in the physical sciences and in philosophy.
tldr: A philosophical and historical essay situating reverse mathematics—the program of identifying minimal set-existence axioms needed to prove ordinary mathematical theorems—within foundational debates in the philosophy of mathematics.
motivation: The author aims to connect the technical classification results of reverse mathematics to broader philosophical questions about foundations, realism, determinacy, and the applicability of mathematics to the physical sciences.
method: Conceptual and historical analysis, tracing reverse mathematics from the foundational programmes of Hilbert and Brouwer to contemporary philosophy, and examining how computability theory measures the strength of set-existence principles.
result: The essay argues that reverse mathematics illuminates central issues in the philosophy of mathematics and clarifies questions about idealisation when set-existence principles are applied outside pure mathematics.
conclusion: Reverse mathematics is presented as a bridge between mathematical logic and philosophy, with implications for debates on realism, determinacy, and applicability, though it offers no quantum-information or thermodynamics content.

title: Data-Driven Control In Infinite-Dimensional Spaces: Fundamental Lemma And Applications
authors: Daniel L\'opez-Montero
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-driven control of dynamical systems has attracted significant research interest. This paper establishes a theoretical foundation for data-driven control in infinite-dimensional spaces by extending the notions of persistency of excitation, data informativity, and Willems' fundamental lemma. These extensions enable their direct application to systems governed by partial differential equations and delay differential equations.
tldr: This paper extends data-driven control theory, including Willems' fundamental lemma and persistency of excitation, to infinite-dimensional systems such as PDEs and delay differential equations.
motivation: Data-driven control has largely been developed for finite-dimensional systems, but many physical systems are governed by infinite-dimensional dynamics, creating a need for a theoretical foundation in that setting.
method: The author generalizes key concepts from the finite-dimensional data-driven control literature—persistency of excitation, data informativity, and Willems' fundamental lemma—to infinite-dimensional spaces.
result: The extended framework enables direct data-driven control design for systems described by partial differential equations and delay differential equations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for applying data-driven control to infinite-dimensional systems, broadening the scope of the fundamental lemma.

title: Comparison Of Two Approaches To Weighted Topological Entropy
authors: Masaki Tsukamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare the Feng--Huang and covering definitions of weighted topological entropy for equivariant continuous maps between dynamical systems. The two quantities agree on the whole space by their variational principles, but need not agree on non-invariant subsets. We prove that the Feng--Huang entropy is bounded above by the covering entropy on every subset, without assuming invariance. The proof does not rely on measure theory. Our main result provides a new perspective on the two relative weighted variational principles.
tldr: This paper compares two definitions of weighted topological entropy for equivariant continuous maps, proving that Feng–Huang entropy is bounded above by covering entropy on arbitrary subsets without invariance assumptions.
motivation: Weighted topological entropy has multiple definitions that agree under variational principles on invariant spaces, but their relationship on non-invariant subsets is unclear.
method: The authors directly compare the Feng–Huang and covering definitions of weighted topological entropy and prove an inequality between them on every subset, avoiding measure-theoretic arguments.
result: The Feng–Huang entropy is shown to be bounded above by the covering entropy on all subsets, even without invariance, providing a new perspective on the two relative weighted variational principles.
conclusion: The two entropy notions need not coincide on non-invariant subsets, and the proven inequality clarifies their relative behavior in dynamical systems.

title: The Inverse Elastic Scattering Problem In The Cavity With Impedance Boundary
authors: Shiyu Xu, Huiling Zheng, Fang Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the elastic inverse scattering problem in a two-dimensional cavity with an impedance boundary condition. We prove that the scattered fields inside the cavity satisfy a reciprocity relation, and prove that both the shape of cavity and the impedance parameter on the boundary can be uniquely determined from the scattered fields measured on an interior curve. Numerically, we first employ the linear sampling method to reconstruct the shape, and then recover the impedance parameter by combining potential theory with the least squares method. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our methods.
tldr: This paper studies an inverse elastic scattering problem in a 2D cavity with impedance boundary conditions, proving uniqueness and providing numerical reconstruction methods.
motivation: The authors aim to determine both the cavity shape and boundary impedance from scattered field measurements on an interior curve.
method: They establish a reciprocity relation and uniqueness result, then use the linear sampling method for shape reconstruction and combine potential theory with least squares for impedance recovery.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed reconstruction approach.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical and numerical framework for inverse elastic scattering in impedance cavities, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Structure-preserving Staggered Semi-implicit Four-split Finite Volume Scheme For Continuum Mechanics On Unstructured Meshes
authors: M. Dumbser, W. Boscheri, M. Tavelli, A. Thomann
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new semi-implicit structure-preserving (SP) finite volume discretization for a unified first-order hyperbolic model of continuum mechanics. This framework provides a common mathematical description for fluids and solids and incorporates transport, viscous effects, heat conduction, and elastic deformations within a single system of hyperbolic partial differential equations. The coexistence of several physical mechanisms gives rise to multiple characteristic wave speeds, resulting in severe time-step restrictions for fully explicit discretizations. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a four-split scheme in which the governing equations are decomposed into convective, temperature, mechanical, and pressure subsystems. The convective subsystem is the only one that is advanced explicitly in time, while the remaining subsystems are treated implicitly in a sequential manner. As a consequence, the time step restriction of the proposed method depends only on the material velocity and is independent of the acoustic, shear, and thermal wave speeds that characterize the model. The scheme is designed to preserve key structural properties of the underlying equations on unstructured grids. In particular, a compatible vertex-staggered spatial discretization on triangles allows the curl-free involutions associated with the distortion field and thermal impulse to be respected whenever the relaxation source terms in the governing PDE are linear or absent. At the same time, the scheme is asymptotic preserving as it is consistent with the low Mach number limit and with the stiff relaxation limits of the GPR model that recover the classical Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations in fluid mechanics. A series of numerical experiments covering both fluids and solids demonstrates the accuracy, robustness, and multi-scale capabilities of the proposed approach.
tldr: A new semi-implicit four-split finite volume scheme for a unified hyperbolic model of continuum mechanics on unstructured meshes.
motivation: To overcome severe time-step restrictions caused by multiple wave speeds in fully explicit discretizations of continuum mechanics models.
method: The governing equations are split into convective, temperature, mechanical, and pressure subsystems; only convection is explicit while the rest are implicit, using a vertex-staggered spatial discretization on triangles.
result: The scheme preserves curl-free involutions, is asymptotic preserving in low Mach and stiff relaxation limits, and demonstrates accuracy and robustness in numerical experiments for fluids and solids.
conclusion: The proposed structure-preserving method enables efficient multi-scale simulation of continuum mechanics on unstructured grids.

title: A Bounded Degree Sos Plus Sonc Hierarchy For Polynomial Optimization
authors: Qi Wang Mareike Dressler
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a bounded degree SOS+SONC hierarchy for constrained polynomial optimization, termed B-SOS+SONC. Starting from Lasserre's bounded-degree SOS framework, we enlarge the certificate cone from SOS to the recently introduced SOS+SONC cone, thereby combining the algebraic strength of semidefinite relaxations with the sparse structure captured by circuit polynomials. We show that, for each fixed certificate degree, the resulting hierarchy is complete, that is, its optimal values are monotone and converge to the global optimum. Moreover, we derive an explicit SDP-REP reformulation, so that each relaxation can be solved within a tractable convex optimization framework over semidefinite and relative entropy cones. Beyond the optimization hierarchy itself, we investigate structural properties of the SONC cone and introduce the notions of first-order and second-order SONC-convexity. This leads to a new sufficient condition for first-level exactness of the B-SOS+SONC hierarchy. Numerical experiments illustrate that the proposed hierarchy often yields tighter lower bounds than the B-SOS relaxation while remaining tractable.
tldr: The paper proposes a bounded-degree SOS+SONC hierarchy for constrained polynomial optimization, combining semidefinite relaxations with circuit polynomials and providing an SDP-REP reformulation.
motivation: Polynomial optimization is a challenging problem, and existing hierarchies like Lasserre's SOS can be strengthened by incorporating sparse structures. The goal is to improve lower bounds while maintaining tractability.
method: The authors extend Lasserre's bounded-degree SOS framework by enlarging the certificate cone to the SOS+SONC cone, derive an explicit SDP-REP reformulation, and analyze structural properties of the SONC cone.
result: The hierarchy is complete with monotone convergence to the global optimum, and numerical experiments show it often yields tighter lower bounds than the B-SOS relaxation while remaining tractable.
conclusion: The B-SOS+SONC hierarchy provides a tractable and tighter approach for polynomial optimization, with new sufficient conditions for first-level exactness via SONC-convexity.

title: Sub-polynomial Parameterized Complexity Of $k$-core
authors: Cristina G. Fernandes Yan S. Couto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The [MATH]-core of a graph is its (unique) largest subgraph with minimum degree at least [MATH]. For any [MATH], deciding whether a given vertex belongs to the [MATH]-core is a P-complete problem, meaning that it is inherently sequential and highly unlikely to admit efficient parallel algorithms, even on graphs of maximum degree [MATH]. This paper investigates alternative parameterizations of the [MATH]-core problem to identify conditions under which it can be placed into sub-polynomial complexity classes. We prove that the problem is in para-NC[MATH] when parameterized by treewidth, and in para-NC[MATH] when parameterized by [MATH] on chordal graphs. Furthermore, we introduce a novel NC[MATH] algorithm for interval graphs when [MATH], which relies on an improved parameterization by pathwidth. Finally, we establish corresponding lower bounds, demonstrating that, even with these parameterizations, computing the [MATH]-core remains L-hard, meaning it requires at least logarithmic space. These findings explore the boundary of parallel tractability for the [MATH]-core problem by highlighting the graph parameters that make it inherently sequential.
tldr: The paper studies parameterized parallel complexity of the k-core problem, showing it lies in para-NC under treewidth and other parameters while remaining L-hard.
motivation: Since deciding membership in the k-core is P-complete and thus inherently sequential, the authors seek alternative parameterizations that could place the problem in sub-polynomial parallel complexity classes.
method: They analyze the k-core problem under parameterizations by treewidth, clique size on chordal graphs, and pathwidth, deriving NC algorithms and corresponding lower bounds.
result: The problem is shown to be in para-NC when parameterized by treewidth and in para-NC when parameterized by k on chordal graphs, with an NC algorithm for interval graphs, though L-hardness lower bounds persist.
conclusion: The work delineates the boundary between parallel tractability and inherent sequentiality for k-core computation, identifying graph parameters that permit efficient parallel solutions.

title: Cobra: A Content-Agnostic Framework For Zero-Day Detection Of Suspicious Domains
authors: Alexandros Fourtounis, Emmanouil Papadogiannakis, Panagiotis Papadopoulos, Nicolas Kourtellis, Evangelos Markatos
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The use of malicious domains is central to cyberattacks such as phishing, malware distribution, impersonation, and fraudulent transactions. Because domains are inexpensive to register and easy to deploy at scale, they remain one of the most common and damaging tools used in cybercrime across industries. Proactive detection is essential to reducing this window of vulnerability and preventing harm to users. In this work, we propose COBRA: a content-agnostic, registration-time detection framework for identifying and analyzing suspicious domains from day zero. Our approach does not rely on any content-based features, allowing us to classify a domain even before it is populated with content. We analyze the names of newly registered domains and employ a clustering technique to group them based on lexical and structural similarity. We evaluate our methodology using real-world data consisting of 1.5M newly created domains, demonstrating that COBRA detects suspicious domains with a precision of 98.5%, identifying more than 47K distinct newly registered suspicious domains. Furthermore, our results show that domain-name clustering enables accurate early detection, allowing us to identify 80% of suspicious or malicious domains earlier than one of the most widely used threat-intelligence services, which in some cases may require up to 7 days.
tldr: COBRA is a content-agnostic registration-time framework for detecting suspicious domains using clustering of newly registered domain names.
motivation: Malicious domains are central to cyberattacks such as phishing and malware distribution, and proactive detection from day zero is needed to reduce the window of vulnerability.
method: The framework analyzes lexical and structural features of newly registered domain names and employs clustering to group similar domains, without relying on any content-based features.
result: On real-world data of 1.5 million newly created domains, COBRA achieves 98.5% precision, identifies over 47,000 distinct suspicious domains, and detects 80% of suspicious domains earlier than a widely used threat-intelligence service, sometimes by up to 7 days.
conclusion: Domain-name clustering enables accurate early detection of suspicious domains, but the work is entirely disjoint from quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: When To Stop? Dynamic Early Termination Of Sequential Ensembles
authors: Paul Bezner, Felix Krieg, Stephan Ten Brink
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ordered-statistics decoding (OSD) post-processing substantially improves the performance of belief propagation (BP) ensembles, but it also removes their natural syndrome-based stopping criterion. The high computational complexity of ensemble decoding and OSD can be reduced by sequential activation of ensemble members paired with an early termination. Instead of a syndrome-based termination we therefore apply dynamic ensemble termination (DET) to sequential ensembles: members are evaluated one at a time and decoding stops when the estimated risk that an unseen member would correct the current decision falls below an offline-fitted threshold. With hardware-oriented design in mind, we instantiate the framework with layered normalized min-sum component decoders, a row-boosted ensemble, conditional low-order OSD on the dual code, and a conventional low-cost decoder gate. A decision tree estimates the residual risk from statistics of the current candidate list. Member-dependent thresholds then target a prescribed frame error rate (FER) loss. We validate this framework on mutliple IEEE 802.11 low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with blocklengths \(648,1296\), and \(1944\) at rates \(1/2\) and \(5/6\). At each code's design point, where the full \(64\)-member list reaches an FER of \(10^{-3}\), the DET decoder processes \(1.04\) to \(1.15\) members on average. On the \((648,540)\) code, it reduces BP work by \(39\times\) and OSD activations by \(18\times\) against the full list while retaining an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain of about \(0.4\,\).
tldr: The paper proposes dynamic early termination for sequential belief propagation/ordered-statistics decoding ensembles of classical LDPC codes.
motivation: Full ensemble decoding with OSD is computationally expensive and lacks a natural syndrome-based stopping criterion after OSD post-processing.
method: Sequential activation of ensemble members with a decision-tree risk estimator, hardware-oriented layered normalized min-sum decoders, a row-boosted ensemble, conditional low-order OSD, and member-dependent thresholds targeting a prescribed FER loss.
result: On IEEE 802.11 LDPC codes, the DET decoder processes about 1.04–1.15 members on average, reduces BP work by 39x and OSD activations by 18x versus the full 64-member list while retaining roughly 0.4 dB SNR gain.
conclusion: Dynamic ensemble termination enables efficient early stopping for classical sequential decoding, but the work is outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: Eigenvectors And Eigenvalues Of $p$-Curvature Operators For KZ--type Differential Connections
authors: Alexander Varchenko Vitaly Tarasov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A KZ-type connection in characteristic [MATH] has [MATH]-curvature operators. These operators are commuting endomorphisms of the connection. We present a Bethe-ansatz-type construction of their eigenvectors and eigenvalues.
