The eigenvector is constructed as the value of a characteristic [MATH] hypergeometric integral and extends to a flat eigensection over the Frobenius neighborhood of the corresponding Bethe point.
tldr: The paper constructs eigenvectors and eigenvalues of p-curvature operators for KZ-type connections in characteristic p using a Bethe-ansatz-type method and hypergeometric integrals.
motivation: p-curvature operators are commuting endomorphisms of KZ-type connections, and their spectral data are of interest in characteristic-p algebraic geometry and integrable systems.
method: A Bethe-ansatz-type construction expresses eigenvectors as values of characteristic p hypergeometric integrals, which extend to flat eigensections over Frobenius neighborhoods of Bethe points.
result: Explicit eigenvectors and eigenvalues are obtained for p-curvature operators of KZ-type differential connections in positive characteristic.
conclusion: The work provides new algebraic and analytic tools for studying KZ connections in characteristic p, but it does not align with the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems interests.

title: Statistical Physics Of Language Change Inferred From Time Evolving Maps
authors: Bert Vaux James Burridge
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language change may be studied by tracking linguistic variant frequencies through space and time. Observed frequencies may be viewed as realisations of a statistical field. We first set out an efficient cross validated method for inferring the empirical field --- the variant frequency distribution estimated directly from data --- in our case, high resolution surveys from 20th century USA. We then derive a model of the statistical field, assuming that individuals diffuse locally, periodically migrate, and copy one another based on a form of replicator dynamics involving both bias and linguistic accommodation. We infer model parameters by comparing changes in model and empirical fields. Our inferences demonstrate that spatial linguistic patterns can be rapidly destroyed by migration but that accommodation can create them, protect them, and in combination with diffusion, produce partially predictable pattern dynamics. The results provide the strongest evidence yet for surface tension driven phase ordering in human dialects. We quantify the model's forecasting ability up to a time horizon of twenty five years using the Kullback-Leibler divergence between forecasts and observations.
tldr: The paper models language change as a statistical field driven by diffusion, migration, and biased replicator dynamics, inferring parameters from 20th-century USA dialect surveys.
motivation: Language change can be tracked through spatial-temporal variant frequencies, but a quantitative inference framework for the underlying social dynamics is missing.
method: The authors develop a cross-validated method to infer empirical variant frequency fields, then fit a statistical field model combining local diffusion, periodic migration, and replicator dynamics with bias and accommodation.
result: Migration rapidly destroys spatial linguistic patterns, while accommodation can create and protect them; the model forecasts dialect evolution up to 25 years using KL divergence, providing strong evidence for surface-tension-driven phase ordering in dialects.
conclusion: Human dialect patterns can be described by statistical physics models of phase ordering, with accommodation and migration playing opposing roles in pattern dynamics.

title: Orbital Optical Chirality As The Origin Of Vortex Dichroism
authors: Keiji Sasaki Yoshito Y. Tanaka
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical chirality quantifies the geometrical twisting of electromagnetic fields and underlies chiral light-matter interactions, yet its conventional formulation captures only the spin-associated chiral geometry of light. We introduce orbital optical chirality and derive its continuity equation, revealing physical properties distinct from those of angular momentum. For vortex beams, spin and orbital optical chiralities follow the spin and orbital indices, respectively. Applied to a twisted nanorod dimer, orbital optical chirality gives rise to vortex dichroism through quadrupolar hybridized modes, while dipolar modes exhibit only circular dichroism. These results establish a unified framework for optical chirality and provide access to chiral geometries beyond those resolved by spin optical chirality alone.
tldr: The paper introduces orbital optical chirality and shows that vortex dichroism in a twisted nanorod dimer originates from quadrupolar hybridized modes, extending optical chirality beyond spin-only descriptions.
motivation: Conventional optical chirality only captures spin-associated chiral geometry, missing orbital contributions that could explain additional chiral light-matter interactions such as vortex dichroism.
method: The authors formulate orbital optical chirality, derive its continuity equation, and apply it to vortex beams and a twisted nanorod dimer to analyze dipolar and quadrupolar mode responses.
result: Spin and orbital optical chiralities follow the spin and orbital indices of vortex beams, and orbital optical chirality produces vortex dichroism via quadrupolar hybridized modes while dipolar modes show only circular dichroism.
conclusion: The work establishes a unified framework for optical chirality that includes orbital contributions, enabling access to chiral geometries not resolved by spin optical chirality alone.

title: Algebraic Proof Of Completeness Of A Positional Numeral System In The Normalized Mersenne Basis
authors: E. Dyachenko
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces and investigates a non-classical positional numeral system constructed on the normalized Mersenne basis [MATH], structurally linking the classical Mersenne sequence (OEIS ) with the integer sequence of alternating binary bitmasks (OEIS ). The main objective of this study is to provide a rigorous algebraic proof of the system's completeness---specifically, theorems on the existence and absolute uniqueness of a canonical representation for any natural number. We show that the internal dynamics of the basis are deterministically governed by the splitting identity [MATH], which strictly restricts the valid alphabet of coefficients to the set [MATH]. Based on the lemma concerning the supremum of lower-order digits and a constructive greedy algorithm, it is proven that the proposed basis forms a closed and unambiguous algebraic space, entirely precluding the overlap of positional masses.
tldr: The paper introduces a non-classical positional numeral system built on the normalized Mersenne basis and provides an algebraic proof of its completeness and unique canonical representation for natural numbers.
motivation: The author aims to extend classical Mersenne number sequences into a rigorous positional numeral framework with well-defined coefficient alphabets and non-overlapping digit masses.
method: Using a splitting identity governing the basis dynamics, a lemma on the supremum of lower-order digits, and a constructive greedy algorithm, the paper derives theorems of existence and absolute uniqueness of canonical representations.
result: It is proven that the proposed basis forms a closed, unambiguous algebraic space in which every natural number has a unique canonical expansion and positional overlaps are precluded.
conclusion: The normalized Mersenne basis yields a well-founded numeral system, though the work remains purely a number-theoretic/algebraic construction with no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ergodic Averages Over Shrinking Sectors Of $\mathbb Z[i]$
authors: Christina Giannitsi Alex Burgin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ergodic averages over Gaussian integers in shrinking angular sectors, which impose an increasingly restrictive directional relation between the real and imaginary coordinates. In uniquely ergodic systems, averages of continuous functions along [MATH] converge to the invariant integral uniformly in the base point and sector location for sectors whose widths shrink subpolynomially in the norm cutoff. For finitely generated multiplicative actions, we prove a quantitative sector--disk comparison in an explicit logarithmic shrinking range, with a power-saving error in [MATH], uniformly in the base point and sector location. The exponents depend only on the number of distinct prime transformations, and the result requires neither ergodicity nor angular-distribution hypotheses on the sets of primes inducing the individual transformations. Strong unique ergodicity then yields convergence to the invariant integral at each fixed base point. Consequences include asymptotic independence of relative angular position and [MATH], Gaussian Liouville cancellation, and joint equidistribution modulo integers of prime-factor counts associated with two prime classes having divergent reciprocal-norm sums.
tldr: The paper studies ergodic averages over Gaussian integers restricted to shrinking angular sectors, proving convergence and quantitative sector-disk comparison results for uniquely ergodic and finitely generated multiplicative actions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how directional restrictions in the complex plane affect equidistribution and ergodic averages, extending classical ergodic theory to shrinking sectors of Gaussian integers.
method: They analyze ergodic averages along Gaussian integers in shrinking angular sectors, using uniquely ergodic systems and finitely generated multiplicative actions with quantitative comparison between sector and disk averages under logarithmic shrinking.
result: They obtain uniform convergence to the invariant integral for subpolynomially shrinking sectors in uniquely ergodic systems, and a power-saving error in a logarithmic shrinking range for finitely generated multiplicative actions, yielding Gaussian Liouville cancellation and joint equidistribution results.
conclusion: The work provides new ergodic-theoretic and number-theoretic results on angular restrictions, but it is unrelated to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Transformer-Informed Trajectory Optimization For Relative Motion In Cislunar Orbits
authors: Walter J. Manuel, Yuji Takubo, Simone D'amico
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous spacecraft guidance and control requires a fast solution to non-convex trajectory optimization, which can be accelerated by providing a near-optimal initial guess to an optimization protocol, i.e., warm-starting. A robust warm starting method is especially useful for rendezvous, proximity operations, and docking (RPOD) in cislunar space, where the underlying dynamics become severely nonlinear and chaotic compared to those in Earth orbit, especially at perilune. This paper extends the Autonomous Rendezvous Transformer (ART), a transformer-based warm-start trajectory generation method, to cislunar RPOD scenarios for the first time. To accurately and reliably solve the nonconvex optimal control problems (OCPs) posed by these scenarios, a new and enhanced version of ART, ART-TWIN (Two-Way INference), is introduced. Inspired by forward-backward shooting methods used in other trajectory design applications, ART-TWIN autoregressively generates two arcs, one from the initial state and one from the desired terminal state, that are patched together at the midpoint of the timeseries. When evaluated on a set of simulated rendezvous scenarios that are initialized at perilune, ART-TWIN is demonstrated to substantially accelerate convergence and increase feasibility guarantees when used as a warm-start to sequential convex programming (SCP), compared to convex relaxations and the original ART. These results illustrate the necessity of ART-TWIN's dual-arc generation to enable the viability of and gain benefits from using transformer-based warm-start methods in the most challenging areas of the cislunar dynamical regime.
tldr: The paper extends the Autonomous Rendezvous Transformer (ART) to cislunar rendezvous, proximity operations, and docking by introducing ART-TWIN, a two-way inference method that generates dual trajectory arcs for warm-starting sequential convex programming.
motivation: Autonomous spacecraft guidance in cislunar space requires fast solutions to non-convex trajectory optimization, and warm-starting can accelerate convergence, but existing transformer-based methods struggle with the highly nonlinear and chaotic dynamics near perilune.
method: ART-TWIN autoregressively generates two trajectory arcs—one forward from the initial state and one backward from the terminal state—and patches them at the midpoint, providing a near-optimal initial guess for sequential convex programming.
result: Evaluated on simulated perilune rendezvous scenarios, ART-TWIN substantially accelerates convergence and improves feasibility guarantees compared to convex relaxations and the original ART when used as a warm-start for SCP.
conclusion: Dual-arc generation is necessary to make transformer-based warm-starting viable and beneficial in the most challenging cislunar dynamical regimes, enabling faster autonomous RPOD.

title: Identifiable Uniqueness Of Impulsively Forced, Inert, And Stabilized Body Trajectories
authors: Bo Pieter Johannes Andr\'ee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An unusual object in the sky raises two related questions: what kind of object it is and what physical process drives its motion. Departures from a gravity-only trajectory can provide evidence, but the same apparent acceleration may be generated by distinct dynamical mechanisms. We formulate this as an identification problem and establish conditions for identifiable uniqueness among three reference classes: inert dynamics, impulsive forcing, and active stabilization such as a controlled spacecraft. The distinction rests on how each class responds to disturbances. Although different mechanisms can produce similar average trajectories, the specified reference models imply different stochastic responses around those trajectories. We show when these differences uniquely determine the dynamical class from the observed trajectory and when several classes remain observationally compatible.
tldr: The paper formulates an identification problem to distinguish inert, impulsively forced, and actively stabilized body trajectories based on their stochastic responses to disturbances.
motivation: An unusual sky object raises questions about its nature and motion, and apparent acceleration alone may be generated by different dynamical mechanisms.
method: The authors define three reference classes—inert dynamics, impulsive forcing, and active stabilization—and establish conditions under which the observed trajectory uniquely determines the dynamical class, using stochastic responses around average trajectories.
result: They show when differences in stochastic responses uniquely identify the dynamical class and when multiple classes remain observationally compatible.
conclusion: Identifiability depends on disturbance responses, providing conditions for distinguishing between natural and controlled motion from trajectory data alone.

title: Maximal Multiplicity Method For Optimal Damping Problem
authors: Maxim Arnold, Oleg Gendelman, Vadim Zharnitsky
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of designing optimal damping for a system of [MATH] coupled linear oscillators. Using the Weyl--Horn theorem, we construct an explicit damping matrix that realizes the optimal asymptotic decay rate of the system. We prove that this decay rate is sharp and is determined by the geometric mean of the natural frequencies. The resulting damping strategy is shown to outperform the classical Rayleigh (proportional) damping approach. We conclude by characterizing the parameter regimes in which the optimal damping matrix necessarily ceases to be positive definite and discuss the implications of this phenomenon.
tldr: The paper constructs an explicit optimal damping matrix for systems of coupled linear oscillators using the Weyl–Horn theorem, achieving the sharpest possible asymptotic decay rate.
motivation: Classical Rayleigh (proportional) damping is standard practice but not optimal for multi-oscillator systems, so the authors seek a provably optimal damping strategy.
method: Using the Weyl–Horn theorem on eigenvalue majorization, they construct an explicit damping matrix and prove the resulting decay rate, given by the geometric mean of natural frequencies, is sharp.
result: The proposed damping outperforms classical proportional damping, and the authors characterize parameter regimes where the optimal damping matrix loses positive definiteness.
conclusion: The maximal multiplicity approach yields a provably optimal and practically superior damping design, with identified limitations tied to loss of positive definiteness.

title: A Multirate Transient Simulation Technique For Circuits Described By Integro-Differential Equations
authors: Kai Bittner Hans Georg Brachtendorf
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multirate partial differential equation (PDE) technique is considered as one of the most powerful methods for the simulation of radio frequency (RF) circuits. The method reformulates the underlying ordinary differential algebraic equation (DAE) by a PDE. The DAE solution is obtained along a characteristic curve of the PDE. Numerical solution techniques comprise (envelope modulated) Harmonic Balance (HB), multistep finite difference (FD) and spline/wavelet techniques. All techniques have disadvantages when mixed lumped/distributed devices occur and the waveforms exhibit pulse shaped behavior. Furthermore, communication systems are modeled and simulated by the Equivalent Complex Baseband (ECB) approach. Signals and impulse responses are described by their baseband counterparts, employing the Hilbert transformation. A coupled system/circuit simulation requires therefore novel numerical techniques for the solution of integro-differential equations.
tldr: The paper presents a multirate transient simulation technique based on multirate partial differential equations for RF circuits governed by integro-differential equations arising in coupled system/circuit simulation.
motivation: Classical numerical techniques such as Harmonic Balance, finite differences, and spline/wavelet methods struggle when circuits combine lumped and distributed devices and exhibit pulse-shaped waveforms, especially when coupled system/circuit simulation requires handling Equivalent Complex Baseband models and Hilbert transforms.
method: The approach reformulates the underlying differential-algebraic equations as a multirate PDE whose solution along characteristic curves yields the DAE solution, extending existing envelope-modulated Harmonic Balance and multistep finite difference schemes to integro-differential equations.
result: The proposed technique provides a numerical framework capable of simulating pulse-shaped, multirate RF circuit behavior where prior methods break down, addressing integro-differential formulations arising from baseband/Hilbert-transform modeling.
conclusion: The work contributes a numerical simulation methodology for RF circuit design and communication system co-simulation, but has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Characterization Of Spatial Topological Chaos For Bistable Lattice Equation
authors: Jakub Hesoun, Petr Stehl\'ik, Jon\'a\v{s} Volek
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The propagation failure phenomenon in bistable lattice equations connects spatial discreteness and weak diffusion to the large number of stationary patterns and the inability of waves to move. We show that there naturally exist bistable lattice equations that do not admit propagation failure for intermediate values of diffusion parameters. The collapse of propagation failure is connected with the existence of a continuum of pinned waves and a continuum of bounded nonmonotone stationary solutions. It also enables us to find explicit forms of traveling waves of families of bistable lattice equations.
tldr: This paper studies propagation failure and spatial topological chaos in bistable lattice equations, showing conditions under which propagation failure collapses and explicit traveling waves emerge.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how spatial discreteness and weak diffusion lead to propagation failure and stationary patterns in bistable lattice equations.
method: They analyze bistable lattice equations mathematically, identifying continua of pinned waves and bounded nonmonotone stationary solutions, and deriving explicit traveling-wave forms for certain families.
result: They find bistable lattice equations that avoid propagation failure for intermediate diffusion parameters, and connect this collapse to a continuum of pinned waves and nonmonotone stationary solutions.
conclusion: The work characterizes spatial topological chaos and provides explicit traveling-wave solutions, advancing the mathematical theory of discrete bistable systems.

title: Adaptive Traffic Camouflage: Causal And Resource-Aware Defense Against IoT Fingerprinting
authors: Daniel Adu Worae, Spyridon Mastorakis, Nuno Moniz, Nitesh V. Chawla
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Encryption hides IoT payloads, but traffic shape can still reveal device identity through packet sizes, timing, direction, and packetization. We present Adaptive Traffic Camouflage, a causal, leakage-aware controller that characterizes traffic-shape leakage without runtime device labels and selects a budget-feasible transformation for the next traffic window from previous-window context. The controller chooses among padding, packet splitting, timing, and composite transformations, or leaves traffic unchanged when camouflage is unnecessary. We evaluate the design on CIC-IoT-2022, IoT Sentinel, and UNSW using classical and sequence-based fingerprinting models under clean-trained, defense-aware, and incremental-exposure settings, with fixed, random, and mean-bandwidth-matched baselines. Under the Balanced profile, camouflage reduces mean Macro-F1 by 13.2-23.3% relative to clean traffic with 4.88-7.47% average bandwidth overhead and at most 0.64 ms added latency. Under the larger Privacy profile, the reduction increases to 28.0-43.5%. Defense-aware training recovers much of the lost attacker performance on CIC-IoT-2022 and UNSW, while IoT Sentinel retains a substantial privacy gap. A non-causal same-window reference provides only modest additional benefit over previous-window control, and metadata-rich attackers remain effective outside the targeted traffic-shape surface. These results show that causal, resource-aware camouflage can reduce IoT traffic-shape fingerprintability under explicit communication constraints, while the persistence of protection depends on how readily the defended distribution can be learned.
tldr: The paper proposes Adaptive Traffic Camouflage, a causal, leakage-aware controller that selects bandwidth-constrained traffic-shape transformations (padding, splitting, timing) to reduce IoT device fingerprinting under explicit resource budgets.
motivation: Encryption hides IoT payload contents but traffic shape (packet sizes, timing, direction, packetization) still leaks device identity, enabling attackers to fingerprint devices.
method: A causal controller characterizes traffic-shape leakage without runtime device labels and picks budget-feasible transformations for the next window based on previous-window context, evaluated on CIC-IoT-2022, IoT Sentinel, and UNSW against classical and sequence-based fingerprinting models under clean-trained, defense-aware, and incremental-exposure settings.
result: Camouflage reduces mean Macro-F1 by 13.2–23.3% (Balanced profile) and 28.0–43.5% (Privacy profile) at 4.88–7.47% bandwidth overhead and ≤0.64 ms added latency, though defense-aware training and metadata-rich attackers partially recover performance.
conclusion: Causal, resource-aware traffic camouflage can meaningfully reduce IoT traffic-shape fingerprintability, but the durability of protection depends on how easily the defended distribution can be learned by adaptive attackers.

title: Refusal Without Discrimination: What Encoded Prompts Do To Safety-Trained Models
authors: Haoyu Zhang, Haowen Xu, Xiao Luo, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Encoded-prompt attacks are evaluated almost entirely on their harmful arm: a benchmark sends obfuscated harmful requests and reports how often the model complied. We show that this arm carries almost no information about the model under test. Across four independently post-trained 7-8B models, refusal of harmful homoglyph-encoded prompts spans 0.08 -- inside the 0.10 ceiling that sampling noise alone produces at n=100 -- while the same four models span 0.57 on the identical requests in plaintext. What the encoding destroys is not refusal but discrimination: on one model the gap between harmful and benign refusal falls from +0.82 in plaintext to exactly 0.00 under the encoding, benign and harmful requests being refused at an identical 0.99. A benchmark reading only the harmful arm scores that model and one retaining a +0.61 gap identically. We then ask whether post-training repairs this, using a published recipe on identical base weights. It does not: across a full SFT -> DPO -> RLVR pipeline, plaintext harm discrimination improves from +0.55 to +0.80 while the encoding-induced loss is unchanged at 0.34-0.50, and on every encoding tested the standard harmful-arm metric moves in the opposite direction to discrimination. None of this is visible without controls the field does not routinely run. We report eight instrument defects, each with the control that caught it; they share a direction, in that every defect on the behaviour axis inflated apparent safety.
tldr: Encoded-prompt (homoglyph) attacks on safety-trained LLMs destroy the model's ability to discriminate harmful from benign requests rather than merely eliciting compliance, so benchmarks that report only harmful-arm refusal rates are nearly uninformative.
motivation: The field evaluates encoded-prompt attacks almost exclusively via the harmful arm (how often the model complies with obfuscated harmful requests), which the authors argue carries almost no signal about the model under test and hides a collapse in harm discrimination.
method: Across four independently post-trained 7–8B models, the authors compare plaintext versus homoglyph-encoded harmful and benign requests, adding the benign control arm, and then test whether a full SFT → DPO → RLVR post-training pipeline repairs the encoding-induced loss.
result: Plaintext harm discrimination spans 0.57 across models while encoded refusal rate spans only 0.08 (within sampling noise at n=100); one model's harmful–benign refusal gap drops from +0.82 to exactly 0.00 (both at 0.99), and post-training improves plaintext discrimination (+0.55 → +0.80) without reducing the encoding-induced loss (0.34–0.50).
conclusion: Standard harmful-arm metrics can be uncorrelated with—or move oppositely to—actual harm discrimination, and eight reported instrumentation defects all inflate apparent safety, showing the need for routine benign controls in encoded-prompt evaluations.

title: Dynamic Deep Prompt Optimization For Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks On LLMs
authors: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Honggang Yu, Xiaolong Guo, Kaichen Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities across many applications but remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which elicit harmful or unintended content. While model fine-tuning is an option for safety alignment, it is costly and prone to catastrophic forgetting. Prompt optimization has emerged as a promising alternative, yet existing prompt-based defenses typically rely on static modifications (e.g., fixed prefixes or suffixes) that cannot adapt to diverse and evolving attacks. We propose Dynamic Deep Prompt Optimization (DDPO), the first jailbreak defense based on deep prompt optimization. DDPO uses the target LLM's own intermediate layers as feature extractors to dynamically generate defensive embeddings via a lightweight multilayer perceptron. These tailored embeddings are then injected into a subsequent intermediate layer, enabling an input-dependent defense without modifying the LLM's weights. This design ensures high adaptability with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on a diverse set of models and attacks demonstrate that DDPO significantly outperforms static prompt optimization methods, particularly on weakly aligned models and when handling semantically ambiguous benign prompts, successfully distinguishing them from genuinely harmful requests.
tldr: DDPO is a dynamic deep prompt optimization defense that injects attack-adaptive defensive embeddings into an LLM's intermediate layers to resist jailbreak attacks without weight updates.
motivation: LLMs remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, and existing prompt-based defenses rely on static prefixes or suffixes that cannot adapt to diverse, evolving adversarial prompts, while fine-tuning is costly and risks catastrophic forgetting.
method: DDPO uses the target model's own intermediate layers as feature extractors and a lightweight MLP to generate input-dependent defensive embeddings, which are then injected into a later intermediate layer, leaving the LLM weights frozen.
result: Experiments across multiple models and attack types show DDPO substantially outperforms static prompt optimization baselines, especially on weakly aligned models and on semantically ambiguous benign prompts that must be distinguished from harmful requests.
conclusion: Dynamic, layer-level prompt optimization offers an efficient and adaptable alternative to static defenses and fine-tuning for LLM safety alignment.

title: A Kernel-Certified Verification Of The Erd\H{o}s-Mollin-Walsh Conjecture Below $10^{14}$
authors: Shayaan Siddique Ibrahim Mian
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erds problem 364 asks whether three consecutive powerful numbers exist, where [MATH] is powerful if [MATH] implies [MATH]. Erds (1976) and, independently, Mollin and Walsh (1986) conjectured that none do; the [MATH] conjecture implies at most finitely many. The conjecture remains open. We present the first verification of the conjecture at any finite bound that is checked end to end by a proof kernel: machine-checked theorems in Lean 4 establishing that no triple of consecutive powerful numbers exists below [MATH] and below [MATH], with the axiom footprint of both theorems being exactly {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} -- no sorry, no native_decide, no trusted external computation. The statements are phrased in the byte-identical vocabulary of the google-deepmind/formal-conjectures formalization of the problem, and we prove abstractly that the open conjecture implies each bounded form, pinning the statement correspondence. The proof reduces the search to odd numbers via a mod-4 argument, represents every odd powerful number as [MATH] with [MATH] odd and [MATH] squarefree, enumerates all odd powerful numbers by a fueled, kernel-reducible generator whose completeness is proved once and instantiated across 3,524 per-interval Boolean certificates, and eliminates the seven surviving distance-2 pairs (the members of OEIS A076445 below [MATH]) by explicit non-powerfulness witnesses. Every certificate's expected values are computed independently by a Python engine, so each kernel-checked equality doubles as a cross-implementation agreement. Total certified kernel time is roughly 46 CPU-hours. Larger uncertified computations exist (exhaustive to [MATH]; conditionally to about [MATH]); our contribution is not a computational record but the elimination of trusted enumeration code from the evidence chain.
tldr: A Lean 4 kernel-certified proof-verification that no three consecutive powerful numbers exist below 10^14, unrelated to quantum information research.
motivation: The Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture on consecutive powerful numbers is an open number-theory problem; the paper aims to eliminate trusted enumeration code from finite verification evidence.
method: The proof reduces the search to odd powerful numbers via a mod-4 argument, represents them as a^2 b^3 with b squarefree, and uses a kernel-reducible fueled generator plus 3,524 Boolean certificates checked in Lean 4 and cross-validated by an independent Python engine.
result: Lean 4 theorems verify the conjecture below 10^14 with axiom footprint {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, and seven distance-2 pairs are eliminated by explicit non-powerfulness witnesses.
conclusion: This is a formal-verification contribution in number theory, not quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Affine Anchors And Cylinder Obstructions In The Three-Dimensional Tingley Problem
authors: Yicen Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a three-dimensional real Banach space and let [MATH] be a surjective isometry. We study the propagation of an affine formula for [MATH] on a relatively open part of [MATH]. A finite family of antipodal distance coordinates propagates a linear anchor except at three explicitly described degeneracies: a facet, an open face-star, or a family of chord cones with a common cylindrical kernel. We prove that, if the norm has no fixed-direction cylindrical open cone, every affine open anchor is linear and global. This yields a source-geometric criterion for the Mazur--Ulam property and covers, among other non-strictly-convex examples, the Euclidean double cone. We also give a segment-saturation criterion which proves the property for every prism [MATH], where [MATH] is an arbitrary real Banach plane. Finally, in the remaining cylindrical regime, we prove that a chord-saturated same-kernel network cannot be confined to one proper projective quotient arc. We then show that this multi-arc difficulty and the transverse-ruled part of producing an initial affine anchor reach the same final obstruction: upgrading norm calibration on an ambient open cone, together with calibration on a few spherical segments, to pointwise calibration of the sphere map on a two-dimensional open patch.
tldr: The paper studies affine anchors and cylindrical obstructions in the three-dimensional Tingley problem for surjective isometries of real Banach spaces.
motivation: The work aims to understand when affine formulas for surjective isometries propagate globally, yielding a geometric criterion for the Mazur-Ulam property.
method: It analyzes finite families of antipodal distance coordinates and classifies degeneracies via facets, open face-stars, and chord cones with a common cylindrical kernel.
result: If the norm has no fixed-direction cylindrical open cone, every affine open anchor is linear and global; this covers examples like the Euclidean double cone and prisms over arbitrary Banach planes.
conclusion: In the remaining cylindrical regime, the obstruction reduces to upgrading norm calibration on an ambient open cone and spherical segments to pointwise calibration of the sphere map on a two-dimensional patch.

title: On A Conjecture Related To Eigenvalue Perturbations
authors: Ren-Cang Li Lei-Hong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In connection with eigenvalue perturbation bounds, Li [Linear Algebra Appl., 278 (1998), pp. 317-326] formulated three minimization problems involving Hadamard products. The third asks how to relate $[MATH][MATH]\|\cdot\|_[MATH]\circ[MATH]G[MATH]\|\cdot\|_[MATH]\|\cdot\|_[MATH]\|\cdot\|_=\|\cdot\|_[MATH]G[MATH][MATH][MATH]c=1$.
tldr: The paper studies a conjecture related to eigenvalue perturbation bounds involving Hadamard products and minimization problems.
motivation: The conjecture arises from Li's earlier work on eigenvalue perturbation bounds, aiming to resolve an open minimization problem involving Hadamard products.
method: The authors analyze the third of three minimization problems formulated by Li, seeking to relate a certain norm of a Hadamard product to the product of norms under a constraint c=1.
result: The abstract indicates progress on the conjecture, though the precise results are not detailed in the truncated text.
conclusion: This is a contribution to numerical linear algebra and matrix perturbation theory, with no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Numerical Invariants And Parameter Recovery For Quasi-Homogeneous Submodules $[z^k-w^\ell]$
authors: Yin Liu, Yufeng Lu, Yixin Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Yang's higher numerical invariants for the quasi-homogeneous submodules \[ M_{k,\ell}=[z^k-w^\ell]\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2), \qquad k,\ell\in\mathbb N,\quad k\neq\ell. \] The Hilbert--Schmidt property and the low-order invariants [MATH] and [MATH] for this family follow from earlier results on [MATH]-type submodules. Our aim is to determine the complete higher-order sequence. Using the weighted homogeneous decomposition associated with [MATH], we construct explicit orthonormal bases for the two defect spaces and determine the exact support of the shifted defect inner products. For [MATH], set \[ A_j=\left\lceil{\ell}\right\rceil, \qquad B_j=\left\lceil{k}\right\rceil. \] We obtain \[ \Sigma_0(M_{k,\ell})={6}, \qquad \Sigma_j(M_{k,\ell})=F(A_j,B_j), \] where [MATH] is an explicitly evaluated symmetric function on [MATH]. The sequence is nonincreasing, tends to zero, and satisfies [MATH]. Hence its strict descent set is [MATH]. This descent set determines the additive semigroup [MATH], while the complete numerical invariant sequence determines the unordered pair [MATH]. The order of the two exponents is not recoverable because of coordinate-swap symmetry.
tldr: This paper computes higher numerical invariants for a family of quasi-homogeneous submodules in the Hardy space H^2(D^2) using explicit orthonormal bases and a symmetric function.
motivation: Yang's higher numerical invariants generalize the Cowen-Douglas theory and provide numerical invariants for submodules of H^2(D^2), with the goal of fully determining such invariants for the quasi-homogeneous family M_{k,l}.
method: The authors use weighted homogeneous decomposition from a natural C*-action to construct explicit orthonormal bases for defect spaces and determine the exact support of shifted defect inner products, yielding closed-form expressions Sigma_j = F(A_j, B_j).
result: They obtain Sigma_0 = 6 and Sigma_j(M_{k,l}) = F(A_j, B_j), where A_j = ceil(l), B_j = ceil(k), and F is an explicitly evaluated symmetric function; the sequence is nonincreasing, tends to zero, and its strict descent set determines the additive semigroup and unordered pair {k,l}.
conclusion: The complete higher-order invariant sequence recovers the unordered pair of exponents in M_{k,l}, while the order is not recoverable due to coordinate-swap symmetry.

title: Open Quadratic Optimization Programs
authors: Alberto Padoan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper studies open optimization programs, that is, parametric optimization programs viewed as open systems, and their interconnection. Each open optimization program is assigned a behavior and interconnection is defined through variable sharing. For a class of open quadratic programs (QPs), we characterize closure and well-posedness under interconnection and, for modules interconnected by adding their objectives, analyze the convergence of a sequential module-by-module solution method, deriving error bounds for the resulting approximation. We further illustrate that the variables through which modules are interconnected indicate an appropriate behavioral description, and each description requires dedicated interconnection rules. This perspective suggests a route toward compositional analysis and design of optimization architectures.
tldr: The paper develops a framework for parametric optimization programs as open systems, characterizing interconnection, closure, and well-posedness for quadratic programs and analyzing a sequential solution method with error bounds.
motivation: Optimization programs are often built compositionally from modules, but a formal systems-theoretic account of interconnection and its effects on solvability and convergence is lacking.
method: Open quadratic programs are modeled as open systems with behaviors defined by variable sharing; interconnection rules are derived, and a module-by-module sequential solution method is analyzed for convergence and approximation error.
result: Closure and well-posedness are characterized for interconnected open QPs, and error bounds are obtained for the sequential solution method when objectives are added.
conclusion: The behavioral perspective suggests a route toward compositional analysis and design of optimization architectures, with different interconnection rules corresponding to different behavioral descriptions.

title: Quantum Rop: Using Quantum Algorithms For Rop Chain Selection In Exploit Construction
authors: Carlos Benitez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum computing threat to cybersecurity is nowadays predominantly framed around Shor's algorithm and its eventual capacity to break asymmetric cryptography. Beyond cryptanalysis, however, quantum computing may also enable other capabilities in offensive security. This work explores one such direction: the application of quantum combinatorial optimization to Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) gadget selection for exploit construction. We formulate gadget selection as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem that captures individual gadget cost and inter-gadget register-clobbering interactions, and solve it using QAOA on real IBM Heron r2 hardware. Applied to a Linux kernel exploitation scenario, the QAOA-selected chain achieves privilege escalation to uid=0 with SMEP and SMAP active. Across eight Linux binaries and 16 benchmark instances, QAOA recovered the lowest-cost valid chain in 11 cases; in the remaining five, it did not recover the optimum, with the failures associated with excessive circuit depth on current limited hardware.
tldr: The paper applies QAOA to solve ROP gadget selection as a QUBO problem on IBM quantum hardware for exploit construction.
motivation: Quantum computing may enable offensive security capabilities beyond Shor's algorithm, so the authors explore quantum combinatorial optimization for Return-Oriented Programming chain selection.
method: Gadget selection is formulated as a QUBO capturing individual gadget cost and inter-gadget register-clobbering interactions, then solved using QAOA on real IBM Heron r2 hardware.
result: The QAOA-selected chain achieved privilege escalation to uid=0 with SMEP and SMAP active; across eight binaries and 16 instances, QAOA recovered the lowest-cost valid chain in 11 cases, with failures linked to excessive circuit depth.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a proof-of-concept use of quantum optimization for exploit construction, but current hardware limitations prevent consistent optimal solutions and the topic lies outside the researcher's core quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: Ramsey Theory And Topological Dynamics Of 0-dimensional Flows
authors: Krzysztof Krupi\'{n}ski, Junguk Lee, Slavko Moconja
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce several Ramsey-theoretic properties of 0-dimensional ambits and obtain their dynamical characterizations. In consequence, we obtain Ramsey-theoretic criteria for triviality and for profiniteness of some important invariants (in particular, of the Ellis groups) of the ambits in question. This yields a criterion for the structural property that each distal minimal factor of the given ambit is a profinite flow. Another result is a criterion for metrizability of the minimal left ideals in the Ellis semigroup. Then we study three specializations of the above abstract context: to first order theories, to definable groups, and to the classical Kechris-Pestov-Todorevi\'{c} theory, recovering known and obtaining new results in each of these contexts.
tldr: The paper develops Ramsey-theoretic properties of 0-dimensional ambits and uses them to characterize topological dynamical invariants such as Ellis groups and profinite flows.
motivation: The authors aim to connect Ramsey theory with topological dynamics of 0-dimensional flows and apply these connections to first-order theories, definable groups, and the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic framework.
method: They introduce new Ramsey-theoretic properties for 0-dimensional ambits and establish dynamical characterizations, then specialize the general framework to several mathematical contexts.
result: They obtain Ramsey-theoretic criteria for triviality and profiniteness of Ellis groups, a criterion for distal minimal factors to be profinite flows, and a criterion for metrizability of minimal left ideals in the Ellis semigroup.
conclusion: The work recovers known results and derives new ones in the settings of first-order theories, definable groups, and Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic theory, demonstrating the utility of the Ramsey-theoretic approach.

title: Prophet Inequalities Beyond Utilitarian Social Welfare
authors: Daniel Halpern, Abhiram Manohara, Alexandros Psomas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the classical i.i.d. prophet-inequality problem, a single item is allocated to one of [MATH] agents who arrive sequentially, with values drawn independently from a known distribution. When an agent arrives, their value is revealed, and the algorithm must immediately allocate the item or continue. The usual objective is utilitarian welfare: the expected value of the recipient. Guarantees for this objective extend to allocating [MATH] indivisible items to sequentially arriving agents with i.i.d.\ additive values. Utilitarian welfare, however, ignores how expected utility is distributed across agents. Motivated by a rich literature in fair division, we instead evaluate an online rule by its generalized [MATH]-mean welfare, which includes utilitarian welfare at [MATH], Nash welfare (the geometric mean of utilities) at [MATH], and egalitarian welfare (the minimum utility) as [MATH]. When the number of items is large, we show that this many-item fair-division problem is captured exactly by a single-item prophet problem evaluated by the [MATH]-mean of agents' expected utilities. We characterize this single-item problem: every online rule is weakly Pareto dominated by a quantile-threshold rule, and an optimal egalitarian rule equalizes agents' expected utilities. We prove that for every [MATH], the online optimum is at least [MATH] times the prophet's egalitarian welfare; by monotonicity of generalized means, the same guarantee holds for every [MATH]. Further, for egalitarian welfare, the optimal ratio converges to [MATH] as [MATH]. Thus, asymptotically, optimizing egalitarian rather than utilitarian welfare costs only about four percentage points relative to the classical utilitarian ratio of [MATH]. Finally, when [MATH], the worst-case competitive ratio converges to zero as [MATH] for every [MATH], showing that the large-item assumption is necessary.
tldr: The paper studies i.i.d. prophet inequalities under generalized p-mean welfare objectives (including utilitarian, Nash, and egalitarian welfare), characterizing optimal online rules and their asymptotic competitive ratios.
motivation: Classical prophet-inequality guarantees focus on utilitarian welfare, which ignores how utility is distributed among agents; the authors draw on fair-division literature to evaluate online allocation rules by generalized p-mean welfare.
method: They reduce the many-item fair-division problem with large numbers of items to a single-item prophet problem evaluated by the p-mean of agents' expected utilities, then characterize optimal online rules via quantile-threshold rules and Pareto dominance arguments.
result: Every online rule is weakly Pareto dominated by a quantile-threshold rule, the optimal egalitarian rule equalizes expected utilities, the online optimum is at least 1/e times the prophet's egalitarian welfare, and the egalitarian competitive ratio converges to about 0.745 (versus 1-1/e ≈ 0.632 for utilitarianism).
conclusion: Optimizing egalitarian rather than utilitarian welfare costs only about four percentage points asymptotically, while without the large-item assumption worst-case competitive ratios degenerate to zero—showing that assumption is necessary.

title: Joint Quantized Precoding And Bit Allocation For Fronthaul-Constrained Cell-Free Massive Mimo
authors: \"ozlem Tu\u{g}fe Demir
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantization-aware precoding for the downlink of cell-free massive MIMO systems with limited-resolution fronthaul. In such systems, the centrally designed precoder must be quantized before being conveyed to distributed access points (APs), creating a strong coupling between precoder design and fronthaul compression. To capture this effect, we develop an end-to-end signal model based on Bussgang decomposition, where the quantization distortion depends explicitly on the precoder coefficients. Building on this model, we formulate a joint precoding and bit allocation problem under per-AP power constraints and a total fronthaul bit budget. We propose an efficient block coordinate descent algorithm that iteratively updates the precoder, receive scaling, and distortion levels. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms uniform bit allocation and quantization-unaware precoding schemes, particularly in fronthaul-limited regimes.
tldr: The paper develops quantization-aware joint precoding and fronthaul bit allocation for downlink cell-free massive MIMO using a Bussgang-based end-to-end signal model and a block coordinate descent algorithm.
motivation: In fronthaul-constrained cell-free massive MIMO, the centrally designed precoder must be quantized before transmission to distributed access points, tightly coupling precoder design with fronthaul compression.
method: An end-to-end signal model based on the Bussgang decomposition is derived, in which quantization distortion explicitly depends on the precoder coefficients, and a joint precoding and bit allocation problem under per-AP power and total fronthaul bit budget constraints is solved via block coordinate descent.
result: Numerical results show that the proposed scheme substantially outperforms uniform bit allocation and quantization-unaware precoding, especially in fronthaul-limited regimes.
conclusion: Jointly accounting for quantization effects in precoder design and bit allocation yields significant performance gains in fronthaul-constrained cell-free massive MIMO systems.

title: String-Monodromy Rigidity From Six-Point Consistency
authors: Jianqi Sheng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can the characteristic monodromy of string scattering be derived from S-matrix consistency alone, without assuming a worldsheet? We show that finite-particle consistency fixes it to a sharply defined extent. In a massless doubly ordered identity model, two exact six-point residues generate a scalar pentagon and the odd Fay identity, forcing every analytic four-point null kernel to satisfy [MATH] and leaving only the linear, trigonometric, and hyperbolic branches. This converts finite-multiplicity factorization into an all-orders constraint normally associated with worldsheet geometry. For a crossing-symmetric target in the opposite KLT module, positive unsubtracted dispersion with nonzero heavy spectral weight selects the trigonometric branch, and moment determinacy fixes the Veneziano germ up to scale. A two-scale counterexample proves that module entrance is an independent input. Our result therefore identifies both a finite-to-infinite rigidity mechanism for string scattering and the precise missing principle needed for a first-principles derivation.
tldr: The paper derives monodromy rigidity for string scattering from six-point S-matrix consistency without assuming a worldsheet, reducing the allowed branches to linear, trigonometric, and hyperbolic.
motivation: The work aims to understand whether the characteristic monodromy of string scattering can be fixed by finite-particle S-matrix consistency alone, addressing a foundational question about the necessity of worldsheet geometry.
method: Using a massless doubly ordered identity model, the author analyzes exact six-point residues to generate a scalar pentagon and the odd Fay identity, then imposes analytic constraints on four-point null kernels and studies dispersion relations in a crossing-symmetric KLT module.
result: Finite-multiplicity factorization forces all analytic four-point null kernels to satisfy a specific condition, leaving only three possible branches; positive unsubtracted dispersion with heavy spectral weight selects the trigonometric branch, fixing the Veneziano germ up to scale.
conclusion: The paper identifies a finite-to-infinite rigidity mechanism for string scattering and highlights module entrance as an independent input, suggesting the missing principle for a first-principles derivation of monodromy.

title: Higher-Order Sensitivity Analysis Of Wasserstein And Adapted Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization Problems
authors: Nathan Sauldubois
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the higher-order expansions of the sensitivities of functionals of probability measures. Building on the work of and , who established the first-order expansion when the functional arises from a stochastic optimisation problem, we extend these results using recent developments in differential calculus on Wasserstein spaces. Specifically, we generalise their approach to broader classes of functionals defined on the Wasserstein space. We provide an explicit formula for the second-order expansion of the sensitivity of a functional with respect to both the Wasserstein and the adapted Wasserstein metrics. Furthermore, we propose a construction method for the higher-order expansion of these sensitivities. Finally, following recent advances by and concerning sensitivity of Distributionally Robust Optimisation under martingale constraints, we also derive higher-order expansions for sensitivities in the presence of such constraints.
tldr: The paper derives higher-order sensitivity expansions for functionals on Wasserstein and adapted Wasserstein spaces, with applications to distributionally robust optimization under martingale constraints.
motivation: It extends prior first-order sensitivity results for stochastic optimization functionals to higher orders using recent advances in differential calculus on Wasserstein spaces.
method: The author provides explicit second-order expansion formulas, proposes a construction for higher-order expansions, and incorporates martingale constraints from distributionally robust optimization.
result: Explicit second-order sensitivity formulas are obtained for both Wasserstein and adapted Wasserstein metrics, along with a general construction method for higher-order expansions.
conclusion: The work advances sensitivity analysis in distributionally robust optimization but is unrelated to the researcher's interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Three-dimensional Blind Deconvolution By CP-parameterized Kernels
authors: Stefan Kindermann Fatoumata Sanogo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of reconstructing a kernel [MATH] and image [MATH] in a blind deconvolution problem from convolutional data [MATH]. We particularly focus on the 3D case, i.e., on volumetric images. The problem is approached by imposing a semiparametric CP decomposition for the kernel and a variational TV penalty for the image. We also discuss a motion blur ambiguity effect, i.e., a nonuniqueness issue of the kernel in the blind deconvolution problem that may appear in certain videos of moving objects. The blind deconvolution algorithm uses an alternating minimization approach with TV regularization for [MATH] and a CP decomposition step for the kernel. These are implemented with positivity projection, kernel normalization, and\textbackslash or causal support projection steps. Several numerical examples for 3D MRI images, hyperspectral images, and a grayscale test video show the effectiveness of the method.
tldr: The paper develops a blind deconvolution method for 3D volumetric images using a CP-decomposed kernel and total variation regularization on the image.
motivation: Blind deconvolution in 3D is challenging due to nonuniqueness of kernel/image factorization, especially for volumetric data such as MRI and hyperspectral images.
method: The kernel is parameterized by a semiparametric CP decomposition, while the image is regularized with a variational TV penalty; the algorithm uses alternating minimization with positivity, normalization, causal support projections, and a CP decomposition step.
result: Numerical experiments on 3D MRI images, hyperspectral images, and a grayscale test video demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and highlight a motion blur ambiguity.
conclusion: The CP-parameterized kernel approach with TV regularization provides an effective solution for 3D blind deconvolution, though it lies outside quantum information and related research directions.

title: High-Order Variable-Scaled Energetic Variational Neural Networks For Phase-Field Gradient Flows
authors: Xiaobo Jing, Leiyi Dong, Jia Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a high-order variable-scaled energetic variational neural network (VS-EVNN) method for phase-field gradient flows. Each discretization stage uses an updated-state network whose spatial inputs are centered and divided by the interface scale, while the sampled energy and movement penalties remain unchanged relative to the baseline EVNN formulation. This rescaling is motivated by a coordinate change in the energy that normalizes the gradient coefficient of the transformed functional. We combine the scaled representation with high-order, multi-stage variational extrapolation schemes and a heuristic adaptive time-stepping controller. Each stage is solved as a network minimization problem, in which the earlier stages serve as fixed anchors on the quadrature grid, yielding a neural realization of these multi-stage variational schemes, including a mobility-weighted, mass-conserving version for Cahn--Hilliard flows. The method is tested on one- and two-dimensional Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard flows, the latter in the mass-conserving metric. Under the reported optimization settings, the scaled networks yield lower solution errors than the unscaled EVNN baseline, and the higher-order schemes improve the accuracy in the test examples.
tldr: The paper introduces a variable-scaled energetic variational neural network (VS-EVNN) with high-order multi-stage schemes for solving phase-field gradient flows such as Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations.
motivation: Standard energetic variational neural networks (EVNN) struggle with accuracy when the phase-field interface scale varies, motivating a rescaling of network inputs and a coordinate change in the energy functional to normalize the gradient coefficient.
method: Each discretization stage uses an updated-state network with spatially centered and scaled inputs, combined with high-order multi-stage variational extrapolation and a heuristic adaptive time-stepping controller; each stage is solved as a network minimization with earlier stages as fixed anchors, including a mobility-weighted mass-conserving variant for Cahn-Hilliard flows.
result: On one- and two-dimensional Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard test problems, the scaled networks achieve lower solution errors than the unscaled EVNN baseline, and higher-order schemes further improve accuracy under the reported optimization settings.
conclusion: The variable-scaled, high-order EVNN framework provides an effective and more accurate numerical solver for phase-field gradient flows, though the work remains a computational applied-mathematics contribution.

title: The Scott-Vogelius Element Is Inf-sup Stable On Freudenthal Meshes For $k \geq 4$
authors: Siqi Ding, Pingbing Ming, Haijun Yu, Quanfan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Scott-Vogelius element is a classical divergence-free mixed finite element for the Stokes problem that has attracted decades of research attention, yet its theoretical framework remains incomplete. In two dimensions, the inf-sup stability on Freudenthal and other regular meshes has been rigorously established. In three dimensions, Zhang established inf-sup stability on Freudenthal meshes for [MATH] in 2011, while numerical evidence indicates that inf-sup stability remains true for [MATH]. In this paper, we strengthen Zhang's approach and prove that the Scott--Vogelius element is inf-sup stable on Freudenthal meshes for every velocity degree [MATH], thereby resolving a conjecture proposed by Farrell, Mitchell, and Scott in 2024. The proof proceeds by explicit constructions on local patches and does not rely on computer verification.
tldr: The paper proves inf-sup stability of the Scott-Vogelius mixed finite element on Freudenthal meshes in three dimensions for all velocity degrees k >= 4, resolving a recent conjecture.
motivation: The Scott-Vogelius element is a classical divergence-free finite element for Stokes flow, but its three-dimensional inf-sup stability was only known for k >= 4 from prior work and partially conjectured otherwise.
method: The authors strengthen Zhang's approach using explicit local patch constructions and avoid computer verification to establish inf-sup stability for every velocity degree k >= 4.
result: They prove that the Scott-Vogelius element is inf-sup stable on Freudenthal meshes for all k >= 4, thereby settling the conjecture of Farrell, Mitchell, and Scott (2024).
conclusion: This completes the theoretical framework for the Scott-Vogelius element on Freudenthal meshes in three dimensions and provides a rigorous non-computational proof.

title: Uniform Approximation Of Spectra Of Linear Second Order Differential Operators Via Discrete Sine Transform Based Discretisation
authors: Oliver K\v{r}enek, V\'{\i}t Pr\r{u}\v{s}a, Rebecca Tozzi, Martin Vejvoda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study various discretisation schemes for the regular Sturm--Liouville operator on a bounded interval and for the Laplace operator on an arbitrary planar domain, in both cases subject to zero Dirichlet boundary conditions. The objective is to identify a discretisation scheme such that the corresponding discretised operator---a matrix of size [MATH]---produces [MATH] eigenvalues that approximate as closely as possible the first [MATH] eigenvalues of the corresponding operator at the continuous level. By means of numerical experiments we examine several conventional discretisation schemes, and we corroborate the known fact that the conventional discretisations fail to achieve the objective, with the failure attributable to the poor approximation of high-index eigenvalues, and, as a result, to the non-uniform spectrum approximation. In contrast, the newly proposed discrete sine transform based discretisation scheme is designed in such a way that it replicates the asymptotic behaviour of high-index eigenvalues, thereby providing the sought uniform spectrum approximation. Of equal significance is the fact that the proposed discrete sine transform based scheme can be, unlike many Fourier transform based methods, applied to non-rectangular domains.
tldr: The paper proposes a discrete sine transform based discretization scheme for uniformly approximating spectra of linear second-order differential operators.
motivation: Conventional discretizations poorly approximate high-index eigenvalues, leading to non-uniform spectrum approximation and failure to capture the full spectrum accurately.
method: The authors study several standard discretization schemes for the regular Sturm-Liouville operator on a bounded interval and the Laplace operator on planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions, then introduce a DST-based scheme and test it numerically.
result: The DST-based discretization achieves uniform spectrum approximation by replicating the asymptotic behavior of high-index eigenvalues, and unlike many Fourier-based methods, it can be applied to non-rectangular domains.
conclusion: The proposed DST scheme provides improved eigenvalue approximation for linear second-order differential operators and extends applicability beyond rectangular geometries.

title: Doubly Exponential Convergence Of The Cyclic Steepest Descent Method For Strictly Convex Quadratics In Arbitrary Dimensions
authors: Ran Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cyclic steepest descent method (CSD) for strictly convex quadratic minimization. CSD repeats, for j consecutive iterations, the exact steepest-descent step size computed at the beginning of each cycle. The only rigorous result for the real algorithm has so far been restricted to two dimensions, where the cycle-starting gradient sequence is known to converge doubly exponentially. For the simplified ("simple") model obtained by discarding bounded logarithmic terms, Dai and Fletcher predicted that CSD is superlinear whenever the number n of distinct eigenvalues is below twice the cycle length m, and linear otherwise. Let A be symmetric positive definite with q distinct eigenvalues, and suppose 2j > q. We prove the superlinear side of this threshold for the real algorithm in arbitrary dimensions, and in fact obtain a faster, doubly exponential, decay. Except for a Lebesgue-null set of initial points, for every kappa below an explicit positive threshold kappa_0, the cycle-starting gradient satisfies ||g_k|| <= exp(-C exp(kappa k)), and the full gradient and iterate errors satisfy analogous bounds with exponent kappa/j after m iterations. This is the first rigorous proof for the real CSD in arbitrary dimensions, including repeated eigenvalues, and confirms the threshold 2j > q (the simple-model prediction n < 2m); the doubly exponential rate is faster than the superlinear one predicted by the simple model. The proof combines arbitrary-reference ratio coordinates, inverse-image volume contraction, thin-band estimates, and a per-component Borel-Cantelli argument.
tldr: The paper proves doubly exponential convergence of the cyclic steepest descent method for strictly convex quadratic minimization in arbitrary dimensions, confirming a threshold condition involving cycle length and distinct eigenvalues.
motivation: The convergence properties of cyclic steepest descent were previously rigorously understood only in two dimensions, while a simplified model predicted superlinear convergence under a threshold condition. This work aims to establish the real algorithm's behavior in arbitrary dimensions.
method: The proof combines arbitrary-reference ratio coordinates, inverse-image volume contraction, thin-band estimates, and a per-component Borel-Cantelli argument to analyze the cycle-starting gradient sequence.
result: For symmetric positive definite matrices with q distinct eigenvalues and cycle length j satisfying 2j > q, the cycle-starting gradient converges doubly exponentially: ||g_k|| <= exp(-C exp(kappa k)) for almost all initial points and kappa below an explicit threshold, with analogous bounds for full gradient and iterate errors.
conclusion: This provides the first rigorous proof of superlinear (indeed doubly exponential) convergence for the real cyclic steepest descent method in arbitrary dimensions, including repeated eigenvalues, and confirms the threshold 2j > q while showing a faster rate than the simple-model prediction.

title: Group Actions, Fixed Points And Orbit Quotients In Lipschitz Spaces
authors: Arindam Mandal
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Lipschitz mappings associated with group actions by similarities, extending the orbit-quotient approach for point-preserving isometric actions. Normalizing by the similarity ratios we obtain isometric representations whose fixed points are character-equivariant Lipschitz mappings. The corresponding quotients by closed spans of orbit differences provide canonical preduals and norm-preserving linearizations, without an amenability assumption. Applications include positively homogeneous, linear, and bilinear mappings. In particular, we prove that the space of positively homogeneous Lipschitz functions form a [MATH]-complemented subspace of the Lipschitz space (strenghthening the earlier existed result) and interpret existing projections onto linear and bilinear mappings as invariant-mean averages. For amenable groups, the same approach yields isometric realizations of the quotient spaces in the biduals of the original linearization spaces.
tldr: The paper studies Lipschitz mappings under group actions by similarities, extending orbit-quotient and fixed-point methods to obtain canonical preduals and linearizations without amenability assumptions.
motivation: The work aims to generalize the orbit-quotient approach from point-preserving isometric actions to group actions by similarities, addressing technical gaps such as the need for amenability.
method: The authors normalize by similarity ratios to obtain isometric representations, then take quotients by closed spans of orbit differences to construct canonical preduals and norm-preserving linearizations.
result: They show that positively homogeneous Lipschitz functions form a complemented subspace, interpret existing projections onto linear and bilinear mappings as invariant-mean averages, and for amenable groups realize quotient spaces isometrically in biduals.
conclusion: The framework unifies and strengthens known results on Lipschitz spaces and group actions, with applications to positively homogeneous, linear, and bilinear mappings.

title: Volumes Of The Strong And Weak Relaxations Of The Uncapacitated Facility-location Polytope
authors: Jon Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lee, Skipper, and Speakman (2018) asked for formulae or asymptotic expressions for the volumes of the strong and weak relaxations [MATH] and [MATH] of the uncapacitated facility-location polytope with [MATH] facilities and [MATH] customers (their Problem~3, ``Texas Hot''). We give exact formulae for all [MATH] and [MATH], and we give asymptotics that hold uniformly as [MATH], whatever the relative growth of [MATH] and [MATH]. The volume ratio satisfies [MATH]. From this, we read off the behavior in every growth regime of [MATH], and we identify a sharp transition at [MATH]. Below it, in a uniformly random point of the strong relaxation, each facility variable is close to [MATH] with high probability, and the ratio grows superlinearly in [MATH]. Above it, in a uniformly random point of either relaxation, each facility variable is asymptotically uniform on [MATH], and the ratio grows linearly in [MATH].
tldr: The paper derives exact formulae and uniform asymptotics for the volumes of the strong and weak relaxations of the uncapacitated facility-location polytope, identifying a sharp transition in the volume ratio at $m = n/2$.
motivation: Lee, Skipper, and Speakman (2018) posed the open problem ('Texas Hot') of finding formulae or asymptotic expressions for the volumes of these two polytope relaxations with $m$ facilities and $n$ customers.
method: Analytical derivation of exact volume formulae for all $m$ and $n$, combined with asymptotic analysis valid uniformly across all relative growth regimes of $m$ and $n$, plus a probabilistic interpretation of uniformly random points in each relaxation.
result: Exact volume formulae are given, the volume ratio exhibits a sharp transition at $m = n/2$: below it, facility variables concentrate near 0 with high probability and the ratio grows superlinearly; above it, facility variables become asymptotically uniform on $[0,1]$ and the ratio grows linearly.
conclusion: The results fully resolve the Texas Hot problem, characterizing the volume behavior of both relaxations in every growth regime and pinpointing the transition threshold.

title: A Posteriori Error Estimates For Variational Inequalities Of The Second Kind In An Abstract Framework
authors: Lothar Banz, Miriam Sch\"onauer, Andreas Schr\"oder
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, an abstract framework is introduced for the derivation of reliable a posteriori error estimators for variational inequalities of the second kind. Under certain conditions (local) efficiency of the error estimators can also be derived. The framework is based on the estimation of a residuum which results from an equivalent mixed formulation and from the replacement of the Lagrange multiplier by its (possibly post-processed) discrete counterpart. The approach is applied to an idealized frictional contact problem and a Mosolov type model problem in an [MATH]-finite element discretization setup. Several numerical experiments demonstrate the broad applicability of the theoretical findings.
tags: variational inequalities of the second kind
tldr: The paper develops an abstract framework for reliable (and locally efficient) a posteriori error estimators for variational inequalities of the second kind, applied to frictional contact and Mosolov-type problems.
motivation: A posteriori error estimation for variational inequalities of the second kind is less developed than for standard variational equations, and a unified abstract treatment is needed to cover diverse nonsmooth problems.
method: The authors estimate a residuum arising from an equivalent mixed formulation, replacing the Lagrange multiplier by its (possibly post-processed) discrete counterpart, and apply the framework within an [MATH]-finite element discretization.
result: Reliability and, under certain conditions, local efficiency of the estimators are proven and demonstrated numerically for an idealized frictional contact problem and a Mosolov-type model problem.
conclusion: The abstract framework provides broadly applicable reliable error estimators for variational inequalities of the second kind, as confirmed by numerical experiments.
keywords: variational inequalities of the second kind

title: Partition-Matched Evaluation Of Community Features Under Distribution Shift In Android Malware Function-Call Graphs
authors: Junru Zhu, Yixin Yang, Xiaoqing Ding, Ruoyu Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph-based Android malware classifiers can lose accuracy under malware-type or family shifts. We test whether mesoscopic organization in function-call graphs provides shift-stable information beyond local degree profiles (LDP), global statistics, lightweight metadata, and size-matched random partitions. Using 15,000 MalNet-Tiny, Common, and Distinct graphs, six Leiden descriptors specified before evaluation, and five optimizer seeds, communities raise Tiny macro F1 from 78.7% to 81.3% but yield 29.4-point source-only Common degradation. One size-matched random partition yields 27.8-point degradation. Across five random partitions, mean degradation is 27.9 points; the 95% two-level bootstrap interval for random minus community degradation is [-4.2, 1.2] points. With metadata, the corresponding difference is -0.2 points with interval [-1.1, 0.6]. Removing modularity raises structure-only Common macro F1 from 51.9% to 53.6%. The tested signature adds IID signal but shows no repeatable shift-stability advantage, demonstrating why mesoscopic graph claims need partition-matched controls and repeated null draws.
tldr: The paper evaluates whether Leiden community features in Android malware function-call graphs provide distribution-shift stability beyond local and global baselines, finding no repeatable advantage.
motivation: Graph-based Android malware classifiers often degrade under malware-type or family shifts, and mesoscopic community structure has been proposed as potentially shift-stable information.
method: Using 15,000 MalNet-Tiny, Common, and Distinct graphs, six pre-specified Leiden descriptors, and five optimizer seeds, the authors compare community-based features against degree profiles, global statistics, metadata, and size-matched random partitions under source-only shift.
result: Communities improve Tiny macro F1 from 78.7% to 81.3% but show 29.4-point source-only Common degradation, similar to random partitions (27.8–27.9 points); bootstrap intervals include zero for random-minus-community degradation.
conclusion: The tested community signature adds IID signal but no repeatable shift-stability advantage, highlighting the need for partition-matched controls and repeated null draws in mesoscopic graph claims.

title: Sled-ifv: Solver-Validated LLM-Guided Decomposition For Scalable Hardware Information-Flow Verification
authors: Liangtao Dai, Yimin Gao, Melika Morsali, Mircea Stan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.25637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formal hardware information-flow verification (IFV) provides strong guarantees against secret-dependent timing and control behavior, but often scales poorly on realistic RTL. We identify two recurring proof barriers in self-composed IFV: implementation complexity, where proof-hard datapath logic dominates even though the property needs only a compact boundary relation, and relational inductive complexity, where the proof depends on cross-copy public-control facts that the backend prover does not infer efficiently. To address them, we introduce two semantic proof decomposition forms: functional simplification, which replaces a proof-hard RTL region with a validated over-approximate summary, and relational strengthening, which exposes and proves the cross-copy relations needed for induction. We further present SLED-IFV, a solver-validated LLM-guided flow that automates the selection of these forms and their concrete targets. Given a self-composed miter and an oracle-free decision sheet, the LLM proposes a decomposition, then materializes it into proof artifacts under controller checks. The controller compiles the checked artifacts into proof obligations, and the formal verification backend remains the sole authority for acceptance. Across nine nontrivial benchmarks constructed from real RTL, SLED-IFV achieves up to 603x solver-only speedup and converts two 12-hour timeouts into completed proofs. The closed-loop flow produces verifier-accepted decompositions for all cases.
